# DF-PROTOCOL-001 Core Protocol and Receipt Model Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use
> `superpowers:subagent-driven-development` (recommended) or
> `superpowers:executing-plans` to implement this plan task by task. Every
> behavior begins with an observed RED test or deterministic source guard.
> Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Implement the slice-1 `PeerReviewedProtocolPackageV1` contract as
strict Rust core types with duplicate-safe JSON transport, deterministic
canonical-CBOR commitments, the acyclic package-root construction, typed
fourteen-state BCTS milestones, and structurally verified external execution
receipt chains without granting binding authority.

**Architecture:** One focused `decision_forum::protocol` module owns wire
primitives, exact package/event/receipt records, structural validation,
canonical encoding, commitments, lifecycle events, and receipt-chain integrity.
JSON is only a strict transport projection; authoritative values are converted
to canonical CBOR where fixed-width hashes, keys, signatures, UUIDs, and Git
object IDs are byte strings and maps use RFC 8949 deterministic key order. The
only opaque outputs are recomputation results (`VerifiedPackageRoot` and
`VerifiedExecutionHistory`). A verified root privately retains its numeric
package version and exact verified predecessor-chain reference so a later
receipt-history consumer cannot splice that root onto an unrelated same-scope
history. Neither opaque result carries seat qualification, kernel approval,
ratification, or execution authorization, all of which remain fail-closed for
later slices.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 2024 / rustc 1.85+, `serde`, `serde_json`, `serde_path_to_error`, `ciborium`
0.2.2, BLAKE3, existing `exo_core::{bcts,crypto,types}` primitives,
`thiserror`, caller-supplied UUID/HLC values, the hardened Rust/TypeScript
cross-implementation harness, Bash, `jq`, `cargo audit`, and `cargo deny`.

## Global Constraints

- Implementation starts from the reviewed slice-1 merge commit, not task base
  `a58a08bfe64c4a987ea0ccb117860e927b6f05a3`. Record the actual reviewed
  predecessor SHA before work; stop if the slice-1 schema, amendment manifest,
  and hardened vector harness are absent.
- Work only on branch `bob-stewart/df-protocol-001-02-core-model` in a clean,
  dedicated worktree. No gateway, database, migration, SDK, WASM, MCP,
  GraphQL, UI, CrossChecked, CyberMedica, publisher, or deployment change is
  part of this slice.
- D9 Amendment 1 is proposed and non-enacting until an independently verified
  exact-hash ratification proof exists. This slice has no API capable of
  returning binding authority. `VerifiedPackageRoot::grants_authority()` and
  `VerifiedExecutionHistory::grants_authority()` return `false` unconditionally.
- Rust is edition 2024 and requires rustc 1.85 or newer. No unsafe code,
  production `unwrap`/`expect`, floating point, `HashMap`/`HashSet`, system
  clock, randomness, or generated governance identifiers are allowed.
- Authoritative collections use `BTreeMap`/`BTreeSet`; ordered vectors have
  documented order and uniqueness checks. Checked integer arithmetic is
  mandatory. Basis points are integers in `0..=10_000`.
- JSON transport uses lowercase hex strings for 32-byte hashes and Ed25519
  verification keys, lowercase 128-character hex for Ed25519 signatures,
  canonical lowercase UUID strings, typed lowercase SHA-1 Git IDs, and
  `{physical_ms, logical}` HLC timestamps. Unknown fields, duplicate JSON
  members at any depth, malformed/non-lowercase hex, invalid UUID/DID text,
  half-null predecessors, duplicate IDs, invalid order, zero where disallowed,
  overflow, and invalid intervals fail closed.
- Authoritative canonical CBOR uses CBOR byte strings for every fixed-byte wire
  newtype (hash 32, key 32, signature 64, UUID 16, SHA-1 20), never their JSON
  text. Every map is recursively sorted by RFC 8949 deterministic ordering
  (shorter encoded key first, then bytewise lexical order); floats and
  non-string map keys are rejected. The same rule is implemented by Rust and
  TypeScript vectors. JSON bytes are never hashed.
- All commitments use a closed domain registry and BLAKE3 over
  `canonical_cbor((domain, value))`. The registry includes the slice-5
  renderer-manifest domain even though this slice does not render artifacts.
- The acyclic sequence is immutable: authorization target, prepublication
  root, independently signed publication authorization, normalized final
  root, then external artifact manifest. Current-version action/monitoring
  receipts are external. Only a successor package commits the completed prior
  execution chain.
- Version 1 has both predecessor fields null. Version 2 and above has both
  non-null, and `prior_version_hash` equals
  `prior_execution_receipt_chain.prior_protocol_version_hash`.
- Signature-envelope proof-of-possession checks against the envelope's key are
  structural only. In-package keys and stored roots are evidence, never trust
  anchors. Slice 3 owns independently sourced key/seat authority, eligible
  unanimity, exact-hash amendment activation, and binding decisions. Slice 4
  owns persistence, APIs, transactionality, tenant ingress, and runtime bypass
  closure.
- Autonomous loop data requires `1 <= max_iterations <= 25`, a nonempty
  success stop, `repeat_failure_limit == 2`, and a nonempty escalation
  destination. The same validation failure observed twice terminates or
  escalates; no workflow prose authorizes another iteration.
- Apache-2.0 and SPDX remain unchanged for core. This slice adds no dependency
  with an unreviewed license, no proprietary adjacent code, no DAG DB change,
  no billing/savings claim, and no thesis acceptance claim.

### Wave 18 specification-predicate table and proof-layer boundary

This table is normative for every type, fixture, schema, validator, vector,
mutation oracle, Rust/TypeScript executor, source guard, and downstream handoff
in this plan. Structural integrity, signer/seat qualification, and binding
authority are three distinct proof layers. Slice 2 authenticates exact bytes
against an independently supplied opaque trust registry and returns only
non-authorizing structural results; Slice 3 alone qualifies the registry and
may construct an opaque authority decision after ratification and kernel
adjudication.

| Predicate | Structural rule owned by Slice 2 | Authority rule owned by Slice 3 | Valid positive | Boundary positive | Valid non-authorizing | Malformed negative |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E-STOP provider threshold | Active provider set is nonempty and provider-only; approvals are its subset; `required = checked ceil(2*n/3)`; stored count/result equal recomputation; evidence has at least two independent classes including non-provider evidence | Active set equals exact ratified roster; votes are qualified distinct AI-IRB seats/providers; evidence classes are independently qualified; kernel/effect creates opaque stop proof | 3/4 plus evidence is `Fired` | 4/4 plus evidence is `Fired` | 2/4 plus evidence is valid `NotMet` and grants no authority | 2/4 claiming `Fired`, non-subset, non-provider in either provider set, wrong required count, or missing/invalid signature fails |
| Peer review disposition | Authenticate and preserve `Approve`, `ChangesRequired`, and `Reject`; exact response/revision/resolution links remain required | Review judgment does not itself create a body vote or authority | Signed `Approve` | Signed `ChangesRequired` with exact links | Signed `Reject` with reasoned response/minority record remains verifiable and non-authorizing | Wrong reviewer/assignment/version/target/context/signature fails |
| Body vote/quorum | Authenticate unique eligible present votes of every supported choice; preserve fixed eligible denominator; recompute approval set/count/floors/result with precedence `EvidenceFloorFailed`, `ProviderFloorFailed`, `NotUnanimous`, `EligibleUnanimity` | Qualify roster, seat, independence, conflict, authority, evidence/provider floors, ratification, and kernel before opaque unanimity | Five exact `Approve` votes | Five votes including one `Reject` recompute `NotUnanimous` | Four valid votes with one missing, or one `Abstain`, remain valid and non-authorizing | Stored approve count/set/result inconsistent with authenticated votes fails |
| Dissent | Cross-bind exact body, seat, source kind/ID/signed hash, version, target, context, signed choice, effect, HLC, and typed signature | Authorization dissent blocks; monitoring dissent creates Chair alert/continuing review; stop precedence/effect remains Slice 3 | Negative body vote with matching authorization dissent | Signed monitoring disposition with matching monitoring dissent | Peer-review `Reject` is preserved without invented body-vote dissent | Detached, Approve-linked, cross-seat/body/version/target/context/choice/effect dissent fails |
| Purpose-specific signatures | Closed domain, payload, target, envelope, signer reference, exact field binding, canonical CBOR hash, and Ed25519 signature are structurally verified | Human status, Chair/investigator designation authority, seat qualification, notifier authority, unanimity, prerequisites, and binding effects | Correct exact-purpose signature | Correct per-destination failed notification attempt remains present | Structurally valid record may still be non-authorizing | Hash-only, missing, duplicate, wrong-domain, wrong-target, replayed, wrong-field, or wrong-key signature fails |
| Trust construction handoff | Private facts/fields/seals/constructors remain in `trust.rs`; Slice 2 has test-only fixtures and no production trust constructor | Exactly one package-private verifier resolves concrete artifacts, calls kernel, accepts only `Permitted`, and constructs the registry | Planned Slice 3 complete verified input + `Permitted` | `Denied` and `Escalated` both typed failures | Slice 2 structural fixture registry grants no authority | Public/raw/sibling constructor or request-carried trust boolean fails source guard |

Every threshold test covers `required-1`, `required`, and `required+1`. Every
authority enum has a valid non-authorizing fixture. Cross-implementation parity
is run only after these specification-derived vectors pass; parity is a
reproducibility result, never the normative oracle.

### Reserved Slice 3 production trust handoff

Slice 2 adds no production stub or constructor for this reserved function. It
freezes the exact future package-private interface in
`crates/decision-forum/src/protocol/trust.rs`:

```rust,ignore
pub(crate) fn verify_independent_authority_context(
    input: IndependentAuthorityVerificationInputV1,
    kernel: &exo_gatekeeper::Kernel,
    verified_at: ProtocolHlc,
) -> Result<VerifiedPackageTrustRegistryV1, ProtocolAuthorityError>;
```

`IndependentAuthorityVerificationInputV1` is package-private, has private
fields and no public constructor, and contains concrete signed/resolved
identity, controller, key, context, validity, conflict, independence, and
authority-chain artifacts rather than booleans or package-carried facts.
Slice 3 owns the implementation and `ProtocolAuthorityError`. It calls
`Kernel::adjudicate`, accepts only `Verdict::Permitted`, and constructs every
private fact and registry entry inside `trust.rs`; `Verdict::Denied` and `Verdict::Escalated` both return typed errors.

The Slice 2 source guard proves that no non-test production constructor exists
yet and that all facts, seals, fields, and constructors remain private. The
future source-guard replacement contract in Slice 3 proves exactly one non-test verifier exists in `trust.rs`, no sibling constructs facts or registries, no
public/raw constructor exists, the kernel call is present, both non-permitted
verdicts fail closed, and tests no longer rely on a privileged authority-capable
alternate path.

### Wave 18 modular semantic preflight and AAR gate

Before the long monolithic validator, run independent fast guards for:
E-STOP set/math/result/signature semantics; review/vote/quorum/dissent
semantics; the closed purpose-signature matrix; trust-constructor ownership;
fence/parse/materialization; and Rust/TypeScript vector-key parity. Any failure
blocks the monolith. Every implementation wave in this slice closes only with
an evidence-backed AAR recording what failed or surprised the team, root cause,
the exact RED/GREEN or review evidence, the concrete guard/brief/control
change, its owner, and the next wave where it applies. Every slice closeout
consolidates its wave AARs and records which controls become mandatory inputs
to the next slice. Prose without a changed guard, test matrix, task brief, or
durable ledger control is not closed. The AAR is an acceptance gate, not an
optional retrospective, and remains separate from implementation approval.

### Wave 19 command-digest gate graph and failure controls

The author wrapper freezes the plan and materialized owner manifest before any
Cargo, Node, parity, or committed-script execution. It records each execution
as a graph node keyed by the canonical digest of frozen plan SHA, materialized
owner-manifest SHA, working directory, relevant environment, executable, and
exact arguments. A duplicate command digest on the same frozen input is a
validator error rather than another evidence point. The retained graph keeps
the genuine Gate-20 RED and focused GREEN, one optimized all-target touched-
crate runtime, one warnings-denied all-target Clippy execution, the distinct
default-profile compilation proof, the Node environment, both real parity
executors, and both committed comparison scripts. Author executions never
serve as independent-validator evidence.

The default remediation controller is `max_iterations = 8`. Its machine-stable
failure signature is `gate + command digest + diagnostic/assertion ID + owner path/symbol`.
A second identical signature stops and escalates before a third execution. If
two distinct failures in one category occur, the next permitted action is a
complete category inventory; another piecemeal correction is prohibited until
that inventory is recorded. A failed frozen wrapper is immutable evidence: do
not edit its assembly or plan mid-run. A correction creates a new frozen plan
SHA and a fresh wrapper attempt, still counted against the eight-iteration
bound.

Every expensive node records exact UTC start, UTC end, monotonic elapsed
nanoseconds, exit status, command digest, frozen plan SHA,
`materialized_owner_manifest_sha256`, and `output_log_sha256`. Missing timing or
digest data is a failed evidence record and is never reconstructed. The final
coverage proof compares the union of retained selected-test manifests with the
all-target manifest, proves the exact Gate-20 test appeared once and passed in
the all-target output, and emits `__DF_W19_COMMAND_DIGEST_COVERAGE__=PASS` and
`__DF_W19_GATE20_ALL_TARGET_PROOF__=PASS`. Gate 20 therefore does not rerun its
immediate full integration suite and is absent from the later literal selected-
test replay; no unique test or environment is removed.

The implementation recomputes every entry hash and predecessor link; requires
chronological order by `(occurred_at, act_kind, act_id)`; dereferences the exact
Git object and content hash; proves exact set equality among chronology,
submitted, unchanged, assigned, sealed-review, revealed, qualified, disposed,
and reviewed artifacts; verifies the signing payload under the distinct domain
`exo.decision_forum.genesis_adoption_signing_payload.v1`; resolves issuer DID,
key, role, tenant, protocol, version, scope, validity, revocation, and conflict
only from `VerifiedGenesisIssuerAuthorityV1`. Semantic validation rejects any of
the three selected current-package ProtocolHash256 roots
(authorization_target_hash, prepublication_root, final_package_root) appearing
in the scanned genesis ProtocolHash256 fields, via the same closed three-root
set carried by ForbiddenCurrentGenesisRootsV1 / CurrentPackageCommitments. A
closeout-index root is a Slice 10 concept and is not fabricated here. The
verified result is cycle-free and always non-retroactive.

The committed Rust, strict JSON Schema, full input vector, TypeScript actual
executor, and mutation oracle include literal cases named
`genesis_omitted_entry_rejected`, `genesis_duplicate_entry_rejected`,
`genesis_reorder_rejected`, `genesis_artifact_set_mismatch_rejected`,
`genesis_current_root_reference_rejected`, `genesis_retroactive_effect_rejected`,
`genesis_wrong_signature_domain_rejected`, `genesis_wrong_signature_target_rejected`,
and `genesis_forged_issuer_key_rejected`. Each mutation changes actual canonical
bytes/hash or returns the exact typed error; TypeScript never copies expected
outputs.

```rust,ignore
pub struct VerifiedEligibleActiveAiIrbRosterV1 {
    seats: BTreeMap<Did, EligibleActiveAiIrbSeatV1>,
    eligible_active_provider_set_commitment: ProtocolHash256,
    ratified_unavailability_and_recusal_policy_hash: ProtocolHash256,
    minimum_provider_floor: u8,
    minimum_independent_evidence_class_floor: u8,
    seal: AuthorityVerificationSealV1,
}

pub fn verify_estop_against_authenticated_roster(
    dispositions: &[EstopDisposition],
    authorization: &EstopAuthorization,
    roster: &VerifiedEligibleActiveAiIrbRosterV1,
    disposition_authority: &VerifiedPurposeAuthorityFactsV1,
    derivation_authority: &VerifiedPurposeAuthorityFactsV1,
) -> Result<VerifiedEstopDerivationV1, ProtocolError>;
```

The verifier resolves each unique seat/provider/key/context/validity/conflict/
recusal tuple against the opaque roster; applies the ratified unavailable and
recusal policy without silently deleting a seat below the provider or evidence
floor; requires exact equality between the roster's eligible active provider
set, `active_provider_classes`, and its commitment; requires exact set/hash
equality between dispositions and signed vote hashes; then computes
`required = checked_ceil_two_thirds(n)` with checked integer arithmetic. It
rejects omission, extra, duplicate, wrong seat/provider/key/context/validity,
conflict, recusal, floor, set, commitment, and result mismatches. The mutation
corpus includes `estop_self_consistent_one_provider_denominator_shrink_rejected`
as well as every `required-1`, `required`, and `required+1` boundary.

```rust,ignore
pub const BLIND_REVIEW_REVEAL_PACKAGE_V1_SIGNING_DOMAIN: &str =
    "exo.decision_forum.blind_review_reveal_package_signing_payload.v1";

pub fn verify_blind_review_reveal(
    assignments: &[ReviewAssignment],
    commitments: &[SealedReviewCommitmentV1],
    sealed_reviews: &[PeerReview],
    gate: &VerifiedBlindReviewRevealGateV1,
    adapter_authority: &VerifiedBlindCustodyAdapterAuthorityV1,
    package: &SignedBlindReviewRevealPackageV1,
) -> Result<VerifiedReviewRevealV1, ProtocolError>;
```

The verifier requires exact unique assignment/commitment/review/entry set
equality, recomputes every opening, verifies each seat-to-ephemeral-key binding
and sealed review signature, verifies custody head/manifest and seal/reveal gate
chronology, and verifies adapter purpose/key/domain/target/package/version/
tenant scope. CrossChecked may assign, custody, and reveal only; it cannot vote,
authorize, sign EXOCHAIN receipts, or hold core private keys. Required tests are
`sealed_field_absence_api_dom_export_log`, `blind_reveal_mismatch_rejected`,
`blind_reveal_omission_rejected`, `blind_reveal_extra_entry_rejected`,
`blind_reveal_duplicate_entry_rejected`, `blind_reveal_early_gate_rejected`,
`blind_reveal_wrong_key_rejected`, `blind_reveal_wrong_domain_rejected`, and
`blind_reveal_wrong_target_rejected`. The strict schema, Rust and TypeScript
full vectors, exports, public DTO fixtures, and log snapshots contain no
pre-reveal seat, attestation, provider, controller, identity, or stable
correlator field.

#### Complete renderer lock and sole safe publication finalizer

```rust,ignore
}

    draft: PeerReviewedProtocolPackageV1,

```

This is the only public finalizer. It proves exact draft/prepublication/
renderer-lock/publisher-purpose/signing payload/signature/authority bindings,
attaches the independently verified `PublicationAuthorizationReceiptV1`,
normalizes only `receipt_manifest.final_package_root`, computes and sets the
single final root, immediately re-verifies it, and returns an opaque finalized
package/root. No downstream crate may call or copy private normalization.
Schema, full renderer vector, TypeScript actual executor, mutation oracle, and
source guard cover every source/binary/compiler/target/image/tool/font/ICC/
template/style/entrypoint/environment/resource/license/notices/SBOM field and
include `publisher_finalizer_wrong_renderer_lock_rejected`,
`publisher_finalizer_wrong_signing_target_rejected`,
`publisher_finalizer_forged_authority_rejected`, and
`publisher_finalizer_duplicate_normalization_owner_rejected`.

#### Dissent non-regression and Wave 20 after-action review

The existing valid negative/missing-vote behavior is retained unchanged and
made a named source-guard contract: `valid_reject_vote_remains_not_unanimous`,
`valid_missing_vote_remains_not_unanimous`, and
`monitoring_dissent_does_not_manufacture_stop`. A structurally valid Reject or
missing vote recomputes `NotUnanimous`; a monitoring dissent creates its Chair
alert and continuing-review evidence without manufacturing an E-STOP. The
contrary earlier audit was stale and is not an implementation input.

Wave 20 after-action review: the surprise was that an internally complete
Slice 2 validator did not inventory downstream consumers before its expensive
wrapper. Root cause was a missing cross-slice semantic interface gate. Evidence
is the Wave 19 blind-custody stop plus the Slice 5, Slice 7, and Slice 10
inventories. The durable changed control is this consolidated downstream-
interface semantic guard, owned by Slice 2 planning and executed before future
slice-plan validation. The first downstream consumer is Slice 3 interface
freezing; Slices 5, 7, and 10 also consume its frozen GREEN digest. The existing
`max_iterations = 8`, same validation failure observed twice escalation,
two-distinct-category-failure inventory, de-duplication, portable command/input/
output digest ledger, Clippy repair, and fail-fast compile/Clippy ordering remain
mandatory and unchanged.


`VerifiedPackageRoot` retains the four private slice-1 scope/root fields
`tenant_id`, `protocol_id`, `protocol_version_hash`, and
`final_package_root`, plus private `protocol_version: u64` and
`verified_predecessor: Option<PriorExecutionReceiptChainReferenceV1>` lineage
facts. Version 1 stores `None`; every successor stores the exact reference
recomputed from the opaque history against which it verified. It has read-only
scope/root accessors, package-private lineage accessors, and no public
constructor.
`VerifiedExecutionHistory` has private fields, is not `Clone`, and has no public
constructor. Its only creation paths are exact version-1 genesis verification
and atomic continuation. Both opaque results expose
`grants_authority() -> false`; slice 3 must consume them together with its own
opaque exact-hash ratification and independently trusted authority results.

`AuthorizationTargetV1` is an exact normalized projection;
`PrepublicationPackageV1` is a private-constructor transparent wrapper over a
package with publication authorization set to `None` and final root zero.
`NormalizedFinalPackageV1` is a private-constructor transparent wrapper with
only final root zero. Current execution receipts cannot be represented in
`ReceiptManifest` and therefore cannot enter the root they name.

## Canonical implementation contract

This is the only execution contract in the plan. The owner listings below are
the complete code applied by the gate that names them; there is no second
task-level base, staging, or commit procedure. Every gate consumes only files
committed by an earlier row. If a later owner needs a new public or
package-private API, stop and amend this frozen interface and every call site
in one reviewed plan change before implementation.

### Wave 18 closed-schema reconciliation before Gate 03

The Slice 1 schema remains the canonical transport schema, but Wave 18 has
identified a bounded correction to types that Gate 03 consumes. Implement this
as an isolated constitutional-governance-schema commit before any Rust model
change. It changes no ratification state. First run the deterministic guard
below against the materialized Slice 1 schema and retain its failure: the
expected RED is a missing `InvestigatorDesignation` definition and unequal
required-field sets for the remaining corrected definitions.

```bash
set -euo pipefail
schema=governance/schemas/peer-reviewed-protocol-package-v1.schema.json
delta=crates/decision-forum/tests/vectors/df_protocol_wave18_authoritative_delta_v1.json
jq -e --slurpfile delta "$delta" '
  def sorted: sort;
  .["$defs"].SignatureEnvelopeV1 as $sig |
  ($sig.additionalProperties == false) and
  (($sig.required | sorted) == ($delta[0].signature_fields | sorted)) and
  all($delta[0].governed_records[];
    . as $row |
    ($row.record | {
      investigator_designation: "InvestigatorDesignation",

    ((.["$defs"][$def].required | sorted) == ($row.top_level_fields | sorted)) and
    ((.["$defs"][$def].properties | keys | sorted) == ($row.top_level_fields | sorted))
  ) and
  (.["$defs"].DispositionBundle.properties.ai_irb_monitoring_dispositions.type == "array") and
  (.["$defs"].DispositionBundle.properties.ai_irb_monitoring_dispositions.items["$ref"] == "#/$defs/AiIrbDisposition") and

' "$schema"
```

Minimum GREEN is the exact closed schema described by the reviewed Wave 18
delta and Rust structs: the eight record definitions have precisely the listed
top-level fields; every embedded purpose signature is the six-field
`SignatureEnvelopeV1`; every HLC uses the existing two-field HLC definition;
every fixed hash/key/signature uses the existing lowercase fixed-byte
definition; all enumerations are closed; and all six declared set fields use
`uniqueItems: true`. `EstopThresholdResult` remains exactly `Fired|NotMet`,
`DispositionChoice` remains exactly `Approve|Reject|Abstain`, and
`DeliveryAttemptStatus` remains exactly `Delivered|Failed`. Add
`DissentSourceKind`, `NotificationSourceKind`, `InvestigatorDesignation`,
`EstopDisposition`, and `PhasePromotionDisposition`; replace the corrected
AAR/RCA, E-STOP, notification, RESET, phase-promotion, dissent,
`DispositionBundle`, and `CommitmentScheme` shapes. No request-body authority,
human classification, eligibility, ratification, or binding effect is added.

Run the guard GREEN, then run `jq -e . "$schema"`, the Slice 1 schema tests,
`git diff --check`, and the exact Rust/schema name guard in Gate 03. Commit only
the schema path. Gate 03 then implements the Rust types against those reviewed
bytes; schema/Rust field-set drift is a hard failure, not a later cleanup.

### Topological reviewer-sized execution gates

Record and commit a distinct immutable gate base for every row. A reviewer may
reject one row while accepting its neighbors, and no GREEN commit may include
a later row's production file or test. The order is strict: full-package JSON
decoding follows all package types; commitments follow types and scalar
validation; trusted graph verification follows commitments; receipt history
follows verified roots and signer registries; cross-language execution follows
every Rust owner.

### Corrected strict wire contract

Every authoritative timestamp field uses `ProtocolHlc`, not native
`exo_core::Timestamp` serde. Conversion to/from the HLC primitive is explicit
inside core logic. Every authoritative JSON array destined for a set is first
decoded as a vector, rejects a duplicate with its object path and element, and
only then becomes a `BTreeSet`; direct serde into `BTreeSet` is forbidden.

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct ProtocolHlc {
    pub physical_ms: u64,
    pub logical: u32,
}

impl ProtocolHlc {
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn new(physical_ms: u64, logical: u32) -> Self {
        Self {
            physical_ms,
            logical,
        }
    }
}

impl From<ProtocolHlc> for exo_core::types::Timestamp {
    fn from(value: ProtocolHlc) -> Self {
        Self::new(value.physical_ms, value.logical)
    }
}

impl From<exo_core::types::Timestamp> for ProtocolHlc {
    fn from(value: exo_core::types::Timestamp) -> Self {
        Self {
            physical_ms: value.physical_ms,
            logical: value.logical,
        }
    }
}

impl ProtocolUuid {
    fn try_from_bytes(bytes: [u8; 16]) -> Result<Self, ProtocolError> {
        Self::validate(
            Uuid::from_bytes(bytes),
            Uuid::from_bytes(bytes).hyphenated().to_string(),
        )
    }

    pub fn parse(value: &str) -> Result<Self, ProtocolError> {
        let parsed = Uuid::parse_str(value).map_err(|_| ProtocolError::InvalidUuid {
            value: value.to_owned(),
        })?;
        Self::validate(parsed, value.to_owned())
    }

    fn validate(parsed: Uuid, original: String) -> Result<Self, ProtocolError> {
        let version = parsed.get_version_num();
        if parsed.is_nil()
            || parsed.get_variant() != uuid::Variant::RFC4122
            || !(1..=8).contains(&version)
            || parsed.hyphenated().to_string() != original
        {
            return Err(ProtocolError::InvalidUuid { value: original });
        }
        Ok(Self(*parsed.as_bytes()))
    }
}
```

`ProtocolUuid::try_from_bytes` is private and fallible. Tests and fixtures use
schema-valid canonical literals such as
`018f0f58-6d7a-7cc1-9b6d-5f5b8c0a1234`; no `[byte; 16]` fixture constructor is
allowed. Add `serde_path_to_error = "=0.1.20"` to the Decision Forum crate (the
version is already locked transitively), run `cargo deny check`, and map typed
conversion failures to the exact nested path.

```rust
use std::collections::BTreeSet;

use serde::{Deserialize, Deserializer, Serialize, Serializer, de};

macro_rules! strict_set_adapter {
    ($module:ident, $path:literal) => {
        pub(crate) mod $module {
            use super::*;

            pub fn serialize<T, S>(values: &BTreeSet<T>, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error>
            where
                T: Serialize + Ord,
                S: Serializer,
            {
                values.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>().serialize(serializer)
            }

            pub fn deserialize<'de, T, D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<BTreeSet<T>, D::Error>
            where
                T: Deserialize<'de> + Ord + std::fmt::Debug,
                D: Deserializer<'de>,
            {
                let values = Vec::<T>::deserialize(deserializer)?;
                let mut result = BTreeSet::new();
                for value in values {
                    let diagnostic = format!("{value:?}");
                    if !result.insert(value) {
                        return Err(de::Error::custom(format!(
                            "duplicate authoritative array element at {}: {diagnostic}",
                            $path,
                        )));
                    }
                }
                Ok(result)
            }
        }
    };
}
```

`decode_protocol_json`
first runs the recursive duplicate-member visitor, then uses
`serde_path_to_error` for typed conversion; it returns
`ProtocolError::TransportShape { path, expected, actual }`. Every nested object,
including `ProtocolHlc`, signature envelopes, Git IDs, rosters, references, and
manifest records, retains `deny_unknown_fields`.

```rust
#[test]
fn uuid_and_hlc_reject_noncanonical_or_unknown_input() {
    for uuid in [
        "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
```

Gate 07 adds this complete full-package test before `strict_set.rs` exists:

```rust
#[path = "support/df_protocol_001/mod.rs"]
mod fixture;

use decision_forum::protocol::{ProtocolError, decode_protocol_json, encode_protocol_json};
use serde_json::Value;

fn duplicate_array_element(
    package: &decision_forum::protocol::PeerReviewedProtocolPackageV1,
    pointer: &str,
    diagnostic_path: &str,
) {
    let mut value = serde_json::to_value(package).expect("fixture JSON");
    let array = value
        .pointer_mut(pointer)
        .and_then(Value::as_array_mut)
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("missing authoritative array {pointer}"));
    let duplicate = array
        .first()
        .cloned()
        .expect("nonempty authoritative array");
    array.push(duplicate);
    let error = decode_protocol_json(&serde_json::to_vec(&value).expect("candidate JSON"))
        .expect_err("duplicate authoritative element must fail");
    match error {
        ProtocolError::TransportShape { path, actual, .. } => {
            assert!(path.contains(pointer.trim_start_matches('/')), "{path}");
            assert!(actual.contains(diagnostic_path), "{actual}");
            assert!(
                actual.contains("duplicate authoritative array element"),
                "{actual}"
            );
        }
        other => panic!("wrong duplicate-set error: {other:?}"),
    }
}

#[test]
fn nested_duplicates_fail_before_authoritative_conversion() {
    let package = fixture::valid_v1_package();
    let encoded = String::from_utf8(encode_protocol_json(&package).expect("fixture transport"))
        .expect("UTF-8 JSON");
    let needle = "\"starts_at\":{\"physical_ms\":";
    let start = encoded.find(needle).expect("starts_at object") + needle.len();
    let end = encoded[start..].find(',').expect("logical delimiter") + start;
    let physical = &encoded[start..end];
    let duplicate_hlc = format!(
        "{}{},\"physical_ms\":{}{}",
        &encoded[..start],
        physical,
        physical,
        &encoded[end..],
    );
    assert!(matches!(
        decode_protocol_json(duplicate_hlc.as_bytes()),
        Err(ProtocolError::DuplicateJsonMember { ref path, ref member })
            if path.ends_with(".protocol_envelope.starts_at")
                && member == "physical_ms"
    ));

    duplicate_array_element(
        &package,
        "/evidence_manifest/independent_evidence_classes",
        "/evidence_manifest/independent_evidence_classes",
    );
    duplicate_array_element(
        &package,
        "/disposition_bundle/council_eligible_set",
        "/disposition_bundle/council_eligible_set",
    );
}
```

The assignment-selected implementation later in this document is deleted in
implementation. `verify_package_root` computes the version hash from the
complete `ProtocolIdentity` before validating any child. It then calls
`validate_context_graph(package, computed_version, authorization_target,
prepublication_root)` (which recomputes envelope, review-bundle, and eligible-
set hashes internally) and, when a
genesis receipt exists, `verify_genesis_adoption_receipt` before final-root
recomputation. The graph validator enforces all of the following with typed
expected/actual/path context:

- every assignment has one roster seat with equal body, attestation hash,
  context-manifest hash, conflict hash, tenant, protocol, and computed version;
- each assignment has exactly one review; each review has exactly one author
  response, revision diff, and resolution linkage; no orphan or duplicate link
  exists;
- review-bundle, envelope, and both eligible-set hashes are recomputed from
  canonical CBOR, never selected from package fields;
- each present Council or AI-IRB vote is unique, eligible-set-bound,
  exact-version-bound, exact-target-bound, context-bound, and signed; zero
  through five present votes per body are structurally valid. Quorum proofs
  preserve the fixed five-seat denominator and recompute their approval set,
  counts, floors, and deterministic result from authenticated votes. Negative,
  abstaining, or missing votes produce a valid non-authorizing package;
  `binding_mode` remains data and `VerifiedPackageRoot::grants_authority()`
  remains false absent Slice 3 exact-hash ratification and trusted authority;
- each review, vote, dissent, quorum proof, Chair intervention, publication
  receipt, genesis receipt, and preauthorization receipt is linked to the
  computed version/root context appropriate to its acyclic stage; every external
  execution receipt repeats the computed current version and final root;
- each successor reference equals an independently verified completed prior
  history and names that prior version/root, while the successor's assignments,
  reviews, votes, Chair records, and external receipts name the newly computed
  successor version/root.

Gate 10 uses this complete registry and graph implementation. Place the entire
following block in `trust.rs`. No sibling module names a fact record, reads a
fact field, or constructs the seal. `commitment/package.rs` calls only the

receipt code calls only `VerifiedAuthorityRegistryV1::verify_receipt_signer`.
