```rust
fn graph_mismatch(
    path: impl Into<String>,
    expected: impl Into<String>,
    actual: impl Into<String>,
) -> ProtocolError {
    ProtocolError::GraphMismatch {
        path: path.into(),
        expected: expected.into(),
        actual: actual.into(),
    }
}

fn verify_signature(
    path: &str,
    payload_hash: ProtocolHash256,
    signature: Ed25519Signature,
    trusted_key: Ed25519VerificationKey,
) -> Result<(), ProtocolError> {
    let key = PublicKey::from_bytes(*trusted_key.as_bytes());
    let signature = Signature::Ed25519(*signature.as_bytes());
    if crypto::verify(payload_hash.as_bytes(), &signature, &key) {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(graph_mismatch(
            path,
            "valid Ed25519 signature from trusted key",
            "invalid",
        ))
    }
}

fn seat_reference(facts: &VerifiedSeatAuthorityFactsV1) -> AuthorityChainReferenceV1 {
    AuthorityChainReferenceV1 {
        binding_kind: AuthorityBindingKind::SeatAuthority,
        tenant_id: facts.tenant_id.clone(),
        protocol_id: facts.protocol_id.clone(),
        actor_did: facts.seat_did.clone(),
        controller_did: facts.controller_did.clone(),
        scope: facts.authority_scope,
        signing_key_id: facts.seat_signing_key_id,
        verification_key: facts.seat_verification_key,
        authority_chain_hash: facts.verified_authority_chain_hash,
    }
}

fn authority_reference(facts: &VerifiedAuthorityFactsV1) -> AuthorityChainReferenceV1 {
    AuthorityChainReferenceV1 {
        binding_kind: AuthorityBindingKind::NonSeatAuthority,
        tenant_id: facts.tenant_id.clone(),
        protocol_id: facts.protocol_id.clone(),
        actor_did: facts.actor_did.clone(),
        controller_did: facts.controller_did.clone(),
        scope: facts.scope,
        signing_key_id: facts.signing_key_id,
        verification_key: facts.verification_key,
        authority_chain_hash: facts.authority_chain_hash,
    }
}

fn roster_entries(bundle: &ReviewBundle) -> [&SeatAttestation; 10] {
    [
        &bundle.council_seat_attestations.openai,
        &bundle.council_seat_attestations.anthropic,
        &bundle.council_seat_attestations.xai,
        &bundle.council_seat_attestations.alphabet_google_gemini,
        &bundle.council_seat_attestations.independent_non_provider,
        &bundle.ai_irb_seat_attestations.openai,
        &bundle.ai_irb_seat_attestations.anthropic,
        &bundle.ai_irb_seat_attestations.xai,
        &bundle.ai_irb_seat_attestations.alphabet_google_gemini,
        &bundle.ai_irb_seat_attestations.independent_non_provider,
    ]
}

fn verify_attestation(
    attestation: &SeatAttestation,
    facts: &VerifiedSeatAuthorityFactsV1,
    verified_at: Timestamp,
) -> Result<ProtocolHash256, ProtocolError> {
    let actual_hash = domain_hash(ProtocolHashDomain::SeatAttestationV1, attestation)?;
    let exact = attestation.tenant_id == facts.tenant_id
        && attestation.protocol_id == facts.protocol_id
        && attestation.seat_id == facts.seat_did
        && attestation.seat_kind == facts.seat_kind
        && attestation.provider_class == facts.provider_class
        && attestation.controller_did == facts.controller_did
        && attestation.signing_key_id == facts.seat_signing_key_id
        && attestation.verification_key == facts.seat_verification_key
        && attestation.context_manifest_hash == facts.context_manifest_hash
        && actual_hash == facts.seat_attestation_hash
        && attestation.valid_from == facts.valid_from
        && attestation.valid_until == facts.valid_until
        && facts.valid_from <= verified_at
        && verified_at <= facts.valid_until
        && attestation.independent_control_proof_hash == facts.independent_control_proof_hash
        && attestation.authority_scope == facts.authority_scope
        && attestation.authority_chain_hash == facts.verified_authority_chain_hash
        && attestation.signature.signing_key_id == facts.controller_signing_key_id
        && attestation.signature.verification_key == facts.controller_verification_key;
    if !exact {
        return Err(graph_mismatch(
            "/independent_trust/seats",
            format!("independently verified seat facts and hash {actual_hash}"),
            format!("package attestation hash {actual_hash}"),
        ));
    }
    let payload = SeatAttestationSigningPayloadV1::from(attestation);
    let digest = domain_hash(
        ProtocolHashDomain::SeatAttestationSigningPayloadV1,
        &payload,
    )?;
    if digest != attestation.signature.signed_payload_hash {
        return Err(graph_mismatch(
            "/review_bundle/rosters/*/signature/signed_payload_hash",
            digest.to_string(),
            attestation.signature.signed_payload_hash.to_string(),
        ));
    }
    verify_signature(
        "/review_bundle/rosters/*/signature",
        digest,
        attestation.signature.signature,
        facts.controller_verification_key,
    )?;
    Ok(actual_hash)
}

impl VerifiedPackageTrustRegistryV1 {
    pub(crate) fn verify_package_graph(
        &self,
        package: &PeerReviewedProtocolPackageV1,
        protocol_version: ProtocolHash256,
        authorization_target: ProtocolHash256,
    ) -> Result<(), ProtocolError> {
        let mut seats = BTreeMap::<Did, (VerifiedSeatAuthorityFactsV1, ProtocolHash256)>::new();
        let mut expected_authority_chain = Vec::new();
        for attestation in roster_entries(&package.review_bundle) {
            let facts = self
                .seats
                .resolve(&attestation.seat_id, attestation.seat_kind)?
                .clone();
            let hash = verify_attestation(attestation, &facts, self.verified_at())?;
            if seats
                .insert(attestation.seat_id.clone(), (facts.clone(), hash))
                .is_some()
            {
                return Err(graph_mismatch(
                    "/review_bundle/rosters",
                    "ten disjoint body-specific seat DIDs",
                    attestation.seat_id.to_string(),
                ));
            }
            expected_authority_chain.push(seat_reference(&facts));
        }

        let council_roster = roster_entries(&package.review_bundle)[..5]
            .iter()
            .map(|seat| seat.seat_id.clone())
            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
        let ai_irb_roster = roster_entries(&package.review_bundle)[5..]
            .iter()
            .map(|seat| seat.seat_id.clone())
            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
        if package.disposition_bundle.council_eligible_set != council_roster {
            return Err(graph_mismatch(
                "/disposition_bundle/council_eligible_set",
                format!("{council_roster:?}"),
                format!("{:?}", package.disposition_bundle.council_eligible_set),
            ));
        }
        if package.disposition_bundle.ai_irb_eligible_set != ai_irb_roster {
            return Err(graph_mismatch(
                "/disposition_bundle/ai_irb_eligible_set",
                format!("{ai_irb_roster:?}"),
                format!("{:?}", package.disposition_bundle.ai_irb_eligible_set),
            ));
        }

        let mut assignments = BTreeMap::new();
        for assignment in &package.review_bundle.assignments {
            // Pre-reveal blind custody: assignment carries no seat_id /
            // seat_attestation_hash. Identity is bound only at reveal and via
            // review signatures against the independently verified seat roster.
            if assignment.protocol_version_hash != protocol_version
                || assignment.blind_assignment_commitment == ProtocolHash256::ZERO
                || assignment.ephemeral_reviewer_key_commitment == ProtocolHash256::ZERO
                || assignment.context_commitment == ProtocolHash256::ZERO
                || assignment.conflict_commitment == ProtocolHash256::ZERO
            {
                return Err(graph_mismatch(
                    "/review_bundle/assignments/*/context",
                    format!("version {protocol_version} with nonzero blind commitments"),
                    format!("assignment {}", assignment.assignment_id),
                ));
            }
            if assignments
                .insert(assignment.assignment_id, assignment)
                .is_some()
            {
                return Err(graph_mismatch(
                    "/review_bundle/assignments",
                    "unique assignment IDs",
                    assignment.assignment_id.to_string(),
                ));
            }
        }
        if assignments.len() != 10 {
            return Err(ProtocolError::Cardinality {
                path: "/review_bundle/assignments".to_owned(),
                expected: 10,
                actual: assignments.len(),
            });
        }
        let council_roles = assignments
            .values()
            .filter(|assignment| assignment.seat_kind == SeatKind::Council)
            .map(|assignment| assignment.review_role)
            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
        let ai_irb_roles = assignments
            .values()
            .filter(|assignment| assignment.seat_kind == SeatKind::AiIrb)
            .map(|assignment| assignment.review_role)
            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
        let expected_council_roles = BTreeSet::from([
            ReviewRole::Governance,
            ReviewRole::Legal,
            ReviewRole::Architecture,
            ReviewRole::Security,
            ReviewRole::Operations,
        ]);
        let expected_ai_irb_roles = BTreeSet::from([
            ReviewRole::RiskBenefit,
            ReviewRole::Monitoring,
            ReviewRole::AdverseEvent,
            ReviewRole::ProgressiveEvent,
            ReviewRole::CorrectiveAction,
        ]);
        if council_roles != expected_council_roles || ai_irb_roles != expected_ai_irb_roles {
            return Err(graph_mismatch(
                "/review_bundle/assignments/*/review_role",
                format!("Council={expected_council_roles:?}; AiIrb={expected_ai_irb_roles:?}"),
                format!("Council={council_roles:?}; AiIrb={ai_irb_roles:?}"),
            ));
        }

        let mut review_ids = BTreeSet::new();
        let mut assignment_review_count = BTreeMap::<ProtocolUuid, usize>::new();
        for (review_index, review) in package.review_bundle.signed_reviews.iter().enumerate() {
            let assignment_path =
                format!("/review_bundle/signed_reviews/{review_index}/assignment_id");
            let assignment = assignments.get(&review.assignment_id).ok_or_else(|| {
                graph_mismatch(
                    assignment_path.clone(),
                    "existing assignment",
                    review.assignment_id.to_string(),
                )
            })?;
            let (seat_id, (facts, _)) = seats
                .iter()
                .find(|(_, (candidate, _))| {
                    candidate.seat_signing_key_id == review.signature.signing_key_id
                        && candidate.seat_verification_key == review.signature.verification_key
                })
                .ok_or_else(|| {
                    graph_mismatch(
                        format!("/review_bundle/signed_reviews/{review_index}/signature"),
                        "trusted reviewer key from independently verified seat roster",
                        review.signature.signing_key_id.to_string(),
                    )
                })?;
            if facts.seat_kind != assignment.seat_kind {
                return Err(graph_mismatch(
                    assignment_path.clone(),
                    format!("seat_kind {:?}", assignment.seat_kind),
                    format!("signer seat_kind {:?} for {seat_id}", facts.seat_kind),
                ));
            }
            if review.protocol_version_hash != protocol_version
                || review.authorization_target_hash != authorization_target
            {
                return Err(graph_mismatch(
                    format!("/review_bundle/signed_reviews/{review_index}/context"),
                    format!(
                        "authenticated supported review disposition, version {protocol_version}, target {authorization_target}"
                    ),
                    review.review_id.to_string(),
                ));
            }
            let digest = domain_hash(
                ProtocolHashDomain::PeerReviewSigningPayloadV1,
                &PeerReviewSigningPayloadV1::from(review),
            )?;
            if review.signature.signed_payload_hash != digest {
                return Err(graph_mismatch(
                    format!(
                        "/review_bundle/signed_reviews/{review_index}/signature/signed_payload_hash"
                    ),
                    digest.to_string(),
                    review.signature.signed_payload_hash.to_string(),
                ));
            }
            verify_signature(
                &format!("/review_bundle/signed_reviews/{review_index}/signature"),
                digest,
                review.signature.signature,
                facts.seat_verification_key,
            )?;
            *assignment_review_count
                .entry(review.assignment_id)
                .or_default() += 1;
            if !review_ids.insert(review.review_id) {
                return Err(graph_mismatch(
                    "/review_bundle/signed_reviews",
                    "unique review IDs",
                    review.review_id.to_string(),
                ));
            }
        }
        if assignments
            .keys()
            .any(|id| assignment_review_count.get(id) != Some(&1))
        {
            return Err(graph_mismatch(
                "/review_bundle/assignments",
                "exactly one signed review per assignment",
                format!("{assignment_review_count:?}"),
            ));
        }

        let reviews = &package.review_bundle.signed_reviews;
        let responses = &package.review_bundle.author_responses;
        let revisions = &package.review_bundle.revision_diffs;
        let resolutions = &package.review_bundle.resolution_matrix;
        if reviews.len() != 10
            || responses.len() != 10
            || revisions.len() != 10
            || resolutions.len() != 10
        {
            return Err(ProtocolError::Cardinality {
            path: "/review_bundle/{signed_reviews,author_responses,revision_diffs,resolution_matrix}"
                .to_owned(),
            expected: 10,
            actual: reviews.len().min(responses.len()).min(revisions.len()).min(resolutions.len()),
        });
        }
        let mut resolution_ids = BTreeSet::new();
        for index in 0..10 {
            let review = &reviews[index];
            let response = &responses[index];
            let revision = &revisions[index];
            let resolution = &resolutions[index];
            if resolution.review_id != review.review_id
                || resolution.comment_hash != review.review_body_hash
                || resolution.author_response_hash != response.content_hash
                || resolution.revision_diff_hash != revision.content_hash
                || !resolution_ids.insert(resolution.resolution_id)
            {
                return Err(graph_mismatch(
                    format!("/review_bundle/resolution_matrix/{index}"),
                    format!(
                        "review={}, comment={}, response={}, revision={}, unique resolution id",
                        review.review_id,
                        review.review_body_hash,
                        response.content_hash,
                        revision.content_hash,
                    ),
                    format!("{resolution:?}"),
                ));
            }
        }
        let response_hashes = responses
            .iter()
            .map(|value| value.content_hash)
            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
        let revision_hashes = revisions
            .iter()
            .map(|value| value.content_hash)
            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
        if response_hashes.len() != responses.len() || revision_hashes.len() != revisions.len() {
            return Err(graph_mismatch(
                "/review_bundle/{author_responses,revision_diffs}",
                "ten globally unique content-hash identities, paired by canonical vector index",
                format!("responses={response_hashes:?}; revisions={revision_hashes:?}"),
            ));
        }

        let review_bundle_hash =
            domain_hash(ProtocolHashDomain::ReviewBundleV1, &package.review_bundle)?;
        verify_vote_body(
            SeatKind::Council,
            &package.disposition_bundle.council_votes,
            &council_roster,
            &seats,
            protocol_version,
            authorization_target,
            review_bundle_hash,
        )?;
        verify_vote_body(
            SeatKind::AiIrb,
            &package.disposition_bundle.ai_irb_votes,
            &ai_irb_roster,
            &seats,
            protocol_version,
            authorization_target,
            review_bundle_hash,
        )?;
        verify_vote_body(
            SeatKind::AiIrb,
            &package
                .disposition_bundle
                .ai_irb_monitoring_dispositions,
            &ai_irb_roster,
            &seats,
            protocol_version,
            authorization_target,
            review_bundle_hash,
        )?;
        verify_quorum_proofs(package, &seats)?;
        verify_dissents(
            package,
            &seats,
            protocol_version,
            authorization_target,
        )?;

        let chair = self.authorities.resolve(
            &package.protocol_identity.chair_did,
            AuthorityScope::ChairInterventionV1,
        )?;
        let publication = package
            .receipt_manifest
            .publication_authorization_receipt
            .as_ref()
            .ok_or_else(|| {
                graph_mismatch(
                    "/receipt_manifest/publication_authorization_receipt",
                    "one publication authorization",
                    "null",
                )
            })?;
        let publisher = self
            .authorities
            .resolve(
                &publication.publisher_did,
                AuthorityScope::PublicationAuthorizationReceiptV1,
            )
            .map_err(|error| ProtocolError::AuthorityChainMismatch {
                path: "/independent_trust/authorities/publication".to_owned(),
                expected: "independently verified publication authority".to_owned(),
                actual: error.to_string(),
            })?;
        verify_chair_and_publisher(package, chair, publisher)?;
        expected_authority_chain.push(authority_reference(chair));
        expected_authority_chain.push(authority_reference(publisher));
        expected_authority_chain
            .sort_by_key(|value| (value.binding_kind, value.scope, value.actor_did.clone()));
        if package.disposition_bundle.authority_chain != expected_authority_chain {
            return Err(ProtocolError::AuthorityChainMismatch {
                path: "/disposition_bundle/authority_chain".to_owned(),
                expected: format!("{expected_authority_chain:?}"),
                actual: format!("{:?}", package.disposition_bundle.authority_chain),
            });
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

trait VoteGraph {
    fn seat_id(&self) -> &Did;
    fn seat_kind(&self) -> SeatKind;
    fn choice(&self) -> DispositionChoice;
    fn protocol_version_hash(&self) -> ProtocolHash256;
    fn authorization_target_hash(&self) -> ProtocolHash256;
    fn review_bundle_hash(&self) -> ProtocolHash256;
    fn eligible_set_hash(&self) -> ProtocolHash256;
    fn seat_attestation_hash(&self) -> ProtocolHash256;
    fn context_manifest_hash(&self) -> ProtocolHash256;
    fn signed_payload_hash(&self) -> ProtocolHash256;
    fn signed_payload_target(&self) -> SignedPayloadTarget;
    fn signing_key_id(&self) -> ProtocolHash256;
    fn verification_key(&self) -> Ed25519VerificationKey;
    fn signature(&self) -> Ed25519Signature;
    fn payload_hash(&self) -> Result<ProtocolHash256, ProtocolError>;
}

macro_rules! vote_graph {
    ($type:ty, $domain:expr, $payload:ty) => {
        impl VoteGraph for $type {
            fn seat_id(&self) -> &Did {
                &self.seat_id
            }
            fn seat_kind(&self) -> SeatKind {
                self.seat_kind
            }
            fn choice(&self) -> DispositionChoice {
                self.choice
            }
            fn protocol_version_hash(&self) -> ProtocolHash256 {
                self.protocol_version_hash
            }
            fn authorization_target_hash(&self) -> ProtocolHash256 {
                self.authorization_target_hash
            }
            fn review_bundle_hash(&self) -> ProtocolHash256 {
                self.review_bundle_hash
            }
            fn eligible_set_hash(&self) -> ProtocolHash256 {
                self.eligible_set_hash
            }
            fn seat_attestation_hash(&self) -> ProtocolHash256 {
                self.seat_attestation_hash
            }
            fn context_manifest_hash(&self) -> ProtocolHash256 {
                self.context_manifest_hash
            }
            fn signed_payload_hash(&self) -> ProtocolHash256 {
                self.signature.signed_payload_hash
            }
            fn signed_payload_target(&self) -> SignedPayloadTarget {
                self.signature.signed_payload_target
            }
            fn signing_key_id(&self) -> ProtocolHash256 {
                self.signature.signing_key_id
            }
            fn verification_key(&self) -> Ed25519VerificationKey {
                self.signature.verification_key
            }
            fn signature(&self) -> Ed25519Signature {
                self.signature.signature
            }
            fn payload_hash(&self) -> Result<ProtocolHash256, ProtocolError> {
                domain_hash($domain, &<$payload>::from(self))
            }
        }
    };
}

vote_graph!(
    CouncilDisposition,
    ProtocolHashDomain::CouncilDispositionSigningPayloadV1,
    CouncilDispositionSigningPayloadV1
);
vote_graph!(
    AiIrbDisposition,
    ProtocolHashDomain::AiIrbDispositionSigningPayloadV1,
    AiIrbDispositionSigningPayloadV1
);

fn verify_vote_body<V: VoteGraph>(
    body: SeatKind,
    votes: &[V],
    eligible: &BTreeSet<Did>,
    seats: &BTreeMap<Did, (VerifiedSeatAuthorityFactsV1, ProtocolHash256)>,
    version: ProtocolHash256,
    target: ProtocolHash256,
    review_bundle_hash: ProtocolHash256,
) -> Result<(), ProtocolError> {
    let expected_set_hash = domain_hash(
        ProtocolHashDomain::EligibleSetV1,
        &crate::protocol::commitment::eligible_set_commitment(body, eligible),
    )?;
    let expected_target = match body {
        SeatKind::Council => SignedPayloadTarget::CouncilDispositionV1,
        SeatKind::AiIrb => SignedPayloadTarget::AiIrbDispositionV1,
    };
    let mut voters = BTreeSet::new();
    for vote in votes {
        let (facts, attestation_hash) = seats.get(vote.seat_id()).ok_or_else(|| {
            graph_mismatch(
                "/disposition_bundle/*_votes/*/seat_id",
                "verified roster seat",
                vote.seat_id().to_string(),
            )
        })?;
        let digest = vote.payload_hash()?;
        if vote.seat_kind() != body
            || vote.protocol_version_hash() != version
            || vote.authorization_target_hash() != target
            || vote.review_bundle_hash() != review_bundle_hash
            || vote.eligible_set_hash() != expected_set_hash
            || vote.seat_attestation_hash() != *attestation_hash
            || vote.context_manifest_hash() != facts.context_manifest_hash
            || vote.signing_key_id() != facts.seat_signing_key_id
            || vote.verification_key() != facts.seat_verification_key
            || vote.signed_payload_target() != expected_target
            || vote.signed_payload_hash() != digest
        {
            return Err(graph_mismatch(
                "/disposition_bundle/*_votes/*/context",
                format!("recomputed {body:?} context and trusted seat key"),
                vote.seat_id().to_string(),
            ));
        }
        verify_signature(
            "/disposition_bundle/*_votes/*/signature",
            digest,
            vote.signature(),
            facts.seat_verification_key,
        )?;
        if !eligible.contains(vote.seat_id()) || !voters.insert(vote.seat_id().clone()) {
            return Err(ProtocolError::Quorum {
                path: format!("/disposition_bundle/{body:?}_votes"),
                expected: "unique present votes from the fixed eligible set".to_owned(),
                actual: vote.seat_id().to_string(),
            });
        }
    }
    if votes.len() > eligible.len() {
        return Err(ProtocolError::Quorum {
            path: format!("/disposition_bundle/{body:?}_votes"),
            expected: format!("zero through {} authenticated present votes", eligible.len()),
            actual: format!("{voters:?}"),
        });
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn verify_dissents(
    package: &PeerReviewedProtocolPackageV1,
    seats: &BTreeMap<Did, (VerifiedSeatAuthorityFactsV1, ProtocolHash256)>,
    version: ProtocolHash256,
    target: ProtocolHash256,
) -> Result<(), ProtocolError> {
    for dissent in &package.disposition_bundle.dissents {
        let source: &dyn VoteGraph = match dissent.source_kind {
            DissentSourceKind::CouncilAuthorizationDisposition => package
                .disposition_bundle
                .council_votes
                .iter()
                .find(|vote| vote.disposition_id == dissent.source_disposition_id)
                .map(|vote| -> &dyn VoteGraph { vote }),
            DissentSourceKind::AiIrbAuthorizationDisposition => package
                .disposition_bundle
                .ai_irb_votes
                .iter()
                .find(|vote| vote.disposition_id == dissent.source_disposition_id)
                .map(|vote| -> &dyn VoteGraph { vote }),
            DissentSourceKind::AiIrbMonitoringDisposition => package
                .disposition_bundle
                .ai_irb_monitoring_dispositions
                .iter()
                .find(|vote| vote.disposition_id == dissent.source_disposition_id)
                .map(|vote| -> &dyn VoteGraph { vote }),
        }
        .ok_or_else(|| {
            graph_mismatch(
                "/disposition_bundle/dissents/*/source_disposition_id",
                "exact authenticated source disposition",
                dissent.source_disposition_id.to_string(),
            )
        })?;
        let expected_context = match dissent.source_kind {
            DissentSourceKind::CouncilAuthorizationDisposition
            | DissentSourceKind::AiIrbAuthorizationDisposition => DissentContext::Authorization,
            DissentSourceKind::AiIrbMonitoringDisposition => DissentContext::Monitoring,
        };
        let expected_effect = match expected_context {
            DissentContext::Authorization => DissentEffect::AuthorizationBlocked,
            DissentContext::Monitoring => DissentEffect::ChairAlertAndContinuingReview,
        };
        if dissent.tenant_id != package.protocol_identity.tenant_id
            || dissent.protocol_id != package.protocol_identity.protocol_id
            || dissent.protocol_version_hash != version
            || dissent.authorization_target_hash != target
            || dissent.body != source.seat_kind()
            || dissent.seat_id != *source.seat_id()
            || dissent.source_signed_payload_hash != source.signed_payload_hash()
            || dissent.signed_choice != source.choice()
            || dissent.signed_choice == DispositionChoice::Approve
            || dissent.context != expected_context
            || dissent.effect != expected_effect
            || (dissent.context == DissentContext::Monitoring
                && dissent.chair_alert_receipt_hash.is_none())
        {
            return Err(graph_mismatch(
                "/disposition_bundle/dissents/*",
                "exact negative signed source/body/seat/version/target/context/choice/effect",
                dissent.dissent_id.to_string(),
            ));
        }
        let facts = &seats[&dissent.seat_id].0;
        let digest = domain_hash(
            ProtocolHashDomain::DissentSigningPayloadV1,
            &DissentSigningPayloadV1::from(dissent),
        )?;
        if dissent.signature.signed_payload_target != SignedPayloadTarget::DissentV1
            || dissent.signature.signing_key_id != facts.seat_signing_key_id
            || dissent.signature.verification_key != facts.seat_verification_key
            || dissent.signature.signed_payload_hash != digest
        {
            return Err(graph_mismatch(
                "/disposition_bundle/dissents/*/signature",
                format!("trusted source-seat key and dissent digest {digest}"),
                dissent.signature.signing_key_id.to_string(),
            ));
        }
        verify_signature(
            "/disposition_bundle/dissents/*/signature",
            digest,
            dissent.signature.signature,
            facts.seat_verification_key,
        )?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn recompute_quorum_result(
    evidence_floor_met: bool,
    provider_floor_met: bool,
    eligible_count: u8,
    approve_count: u8,
) -> QuorumResult {
    if !evidence_floor_met {
        QuorumResult::EvidenceFloorFailed
    } else if !provider_floor_met {
        QuorumResult::ProviderFloorFailed
    } else if approve_count != eligible_count {
        QuorumResult::NotUnanimous
    } else {
        QuorumResult::EligibleUnanimity
    }
}

fn verify_quorum_proofs(
    package: &PeerReviewedProtocolPackageV1,
    seats: &BTreeMap<Did, (VerifiedSeatAuthorityFactsV1, ProtocolHash256)>,
) -> Result<(), ProtocolError> {
    let required_providers = BTreeSet::from([
        ProviderClass::OpenAI,
        ProviderClass::Anthropic,
        ProviderClass::XAi,
        ProviderClass::AlphabetGoogleGemini,
    ]);
    for body in [SeatKind::Council, SeatKind::AiIrb] {
        let proof = package
            .disposition_bundle
            .quorum_proofs
            .iter()
            .filter(|value| value.seat_kind == body)
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        if proof.len() != 1 {
            return Err(ProtocolError::Quorum {
                path: "/disposition_bundle/quorum_proofs".to_owned(),
                expected: format!("one {body:?} proof"),
                actual: format!("{}", proof.len()),
            });
        }
        let proof = proof[0];
        let eligible = match body {
            SeatKind::Council => &package.disposition_bundle.council_eligible_set,
            SeatKind::AiIrb => &package.disposition_bundle.ai_irb_eligible_set,
        };
        let expected_hashes = eligible
            .iter()
            .map(|did| seats[did].1)
            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
        let approve_hashes = match body {
            SeatKind::Council => package
                .disposition_bundle
                .council_votes
                .iter()
                .filter(|vote| vote.choice == DispositionChoice::Approve)
                .map(|vote| seats[&vote.seat_id].1)
                .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>(),
            SeatKind::AiIrb => package
                .disposition_bundle
                .ai_irb_votes
                .iter()
                .filter(|vote| vote.choice == DispositionChoice::Approve)
                .map(|vote| seats[&vote.seat_id].1)
                .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>(),
        };
        let provider_classes = eligible
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|did| {
                let provider = seats[did].0.provider_class;
                (provider != ProviderClass::IndependentNonProvider).then_some(provider)
            })
            .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
        let eligible_count = u8::try_from(expected_hashes.len()).map_err(|_| {
            ProtocolError::Quorum {
                path: format!("/disposition_bundle/quorum_proofs/{body:?}/eligible_count"),
                expected: "eligible count representable as u8".to_owned(),
                actual: expected_hashes.len().to_string(),
            }
        })?;
        let approve_count = u8::try_from(approve_hashes.len()).map_err(|_| {
            ProtocolError::Quorum {
                path: format!("/disposition_bundle/quorum_proofs/{body:?}/approve_count"),
                expected: "approve count representable as u8".to_owned(),
                actual: approve_hashes.len().to_string(),
            }
        })?;
        let provider_floor_met = provider_classes == required_providers;
        let evidence_floor_met = proof.evidence_classes.len() >= 2
            && proof
                .evidence_classes
                .contains(&IndependentEvidenceClass::IndependentNonProviderEvidence);
        let expected_result = recompute_quorum_result(
            evidence_floor_met,
            provider_floor_met,
            eligible_count,
            approve_count,
        );
        let mut normalized = (*proof).clone();
        normalized.proof_hash = ProtocolHash256::ZERO;
        let recomputed = domain_hash(ProtocolHashDomain::QuorumProofV1, &normalized)?;
        if proof.eligible_seat_hashes != expected_hashes
            || proof.approve_seat_hashes != approve_hashes
            || expected_hashes.len() != 5
            || proof.eligible_count != eligible_count
            || proof.approve_count != approve_count
            || proof.required_count != eligible_count
            || proof.result != expected_result
            || proof.provider_classes != provider_classes
            || proof.proof_hash != recomputed
            || proof.evidence_classes != package.evidence_manifest.independent_evidence_classes
        {
            return Err(ProtocolError::Quorum {
                path: format!("/disposition_bundle/quorum_proofs/{body:?}"),
                expected: format!(
                    "eligible={expected_hashes:?}, approve={approve_hashes:?}, hash={recomputed}"
                ),
                actual: format!("{proof:?}"),
            });
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn verify_chair_and_publisher(
    package: &PeerReviewedProtocolPackageV1,
    chair: &VerifiedAuthorityFactsV1,
    publisher: &VerifiedAuthorityFactsV1,
) -> Result<(), ProtocolError> {
    let authority = &package.protocol_identity.chair_authority;
    if authority.chair_did != chair.actor_did
        || authority.signing_key_id != chair.signing_key_id
        || authority.verification_key != chair.verification_key
        || authority.authority_chain_hash != chair.authority_chain_hash
    {
        return Err(graph_mismatch(
            "/protocol_identity/chair_authority",
            format!("{chair:?}"),
            format!("{authority:?}"),
        ));
    }
    for (index, intervention) in package
        .disposition_bundle
        .chair_interventions
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
    {
        let path = format!("/disposition_bundle/chair_interventions/{index}/chair_did",);
        let digest = domain_hash(
            ProtocolHashDomain::ChairInterventionSigningPayloadV1,
            &ChairInterventionSigningPayloadV1::from(intervention),
        )?;
        if intervention.chair_did != chair.actor_did
            || intervention.signature.signing_key_id != chair.signing_key_id
            || intervention.signature.verification_key != chair.verification_key
            || intervention.signature.signed_payload_hash != digest
        {
            return Err(graph_mismatch(
                path.clone(),
                format!("trusted Chair DID {} and digest {digest}", chair.actor_did),
                format!(
                    "DID {} intervention {}",
                    intervention.chair_did, intervention.intervention_id
                ),
            ));
        }
        verify_signature(
            &path,
            digest,
            intervention.signature.signature,
            chair.verification_key,
        )?;
    }
    let publication = package
        .receipt_manifest
        .publication_authorization_receipt
        .as_ref()
        .ok_or_else(|| {
            graph_mismatch(
                "/receipt_manifest/publication_authorization_receipt",
                "present",
                "null",
            )
        })?;
    if publication.publisher_did != publisher.actor_did
        || publication.publisher_authority.signing_key_id != publisher.signing_key_id
        || publication.publisher_authority.verification_key != publisher.verification_key
        || publication.publisher_authority.authority_chain_hash != publisher.authority_chain_hash
        || publication.signature.signing_key_id != publisher.signing_key_id
        || publication.signature.verification_key != publisher.verification_key
    {
        return Err(graph_mismatch(
            "/receipt_manifest/publication_authorization_receipt/publisher_authority",
            format!("{publisher:?}"),
            format!("{:?}", publication.publisher_authority),
        ));
    }
    let digest = publication_authorization_payload_hash(publication)?;
    if publication.signature.signed_payload_hash != digest {
        return Err(graph_mismatch(
            "/receipt_manifest/publication_authorization_receipt/signature/signed_payload_hash",
            digest.to_string(),
            publication.signature.signed_payload_hash.to_string(),
        ));
    }
    verify_signature(
        "/receipt_manifest/publication_authorization_receipt/signature",
        digest,
        publication.signature.signature,
        publisher.verification_key,
    )?;
    Ok(())
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct VerifiedGenesisIssuerAuthorityFieldsV1 {
    tenant_id: String,
    protocol_id: String,
    protocol_version_hash: ProtocolHash256,
    issuer_did: Did,
    scope: AuthorityScope,
    signing_key_id: ProtocolHash256,
    verification_key: Ed25519VerificationKey,
    valid_from: Timestamp,
    valid_until: Timestamp,
    revocation_hash: Option<ProtocolHash256>,
    conflict_disposition_hash: Option<ProtocolHash256>,
}

/// Opaque output of the (Slice 3) genesis-issuer identity, role, tenant,
/// protocol, version, scope, validity, revocation, and conflict checks. No
/// sibling module names this fact record or reads a field directly.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct VerifiedGenesisIssuerAuthorityV1 {
    private: VerifiedGenesisIssuerAuthorityFieldsV1,
}

impl VerifiedGenesisIssuerAuthorityV1 {
    #[cfg(test)]
    fn from_independent_verification(
        _seal: &IndependentAuthorityVerificationSealV1,
        fields: VerifiedGenesisIssuerAuthorityFieldsV1,
    ) -> Self {
        Self { private: fields }
    }

    fn verify_binding(&self, receipt: &GenesisAdoptionReceipt) -> Result<(), ProtocolError> {
        let facts = &self.private;
        let exact = facts.tenant_id == receipt.tenant_id
            && facts.protocol_id == receipt.protocol_id
            && facts.protocol_version_hash == receipt.protocol_version_hash
            && facts.issuer_did == receipt.issuer_did
            && facts.scope == AuthorityScope::GenesisAdoptionReceiptV1
            && facts.signing_key_id == receipt.issuer_key_id
            && facts.verification_key == receipt.signature.verification_key
            && facts.valid_from <= receipt.effect_starts_at
            && receipt.effect_starts_at <= facts.valid_until
            && facts.revocation_hash.is_none()
            && facts.conflict_disposition_hash.is_none();
        if exact {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(graph_mismatch(
                "/receipt_manifest/genesis_adoption_receipt/issuer_did",
                format!("{facts:?}"),
                format!(
                    "issuer {} key {} at {:?}",
                    receipt.issuer_did, receipt.issuer_key_id, receipt.effect_starts_at
                ),
            ))
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct VerifiedHistoricalArtifactFieldsV1 {
    content_hash: ProtocolHash256,
    path_hash: ProtocolHash256,
}

/// Opaque output of independently dereferencing a Git object to its exact
/// content and path hash. No sibling module names this fact record or reads
/// a field directly.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct VerifiedHistoricalArtifactV1 {
    private: VerifiedHistoricalArtifactFieldsV1,
}

impl VerifiedHistoricalArtifactV1 {
    #[cfg(test)]
    fn from_independent_verification(
        _seal: &IndependentAuthorityVerificationSealV1,
        content_hash: ProtocolHash256,
        path_hash: ProtocolHash256,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            private: VerifiedHistoricalArtifactFieldsV1 {
                content_hash,
                path_hash,
            },
        }
    }

    fn matches(&self, content_hash: ProtocolHash256, path_hash: ProtocolHash256) -> bool {
        self.private.content_hash == content_hash && self.private.path_hash == path_hash
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct VerifiedHistoricalReviewRevealFieldsV1 {
    assignment_hashes: BTreeSet<ProtocolHash256>,
    assignment_commitment_hashes: BTreeSet<ProtocolHash256>,
    sealed_review_hashes: BTreeSet<ProtocolHash256>,
    verified_reveal_hash: ProtocolHash256,
    reviewer_qualification_hashes: BTreeSet<ProtocolHash256>,
    disposition_hashes: BTreeSet<ProtocolHash256>,
    reviewed_artifact_set_hash: ProtocolHash256,
}

/// Opaque output of an independent blind review reveal verification, scoped
/// exactly to the fields genesis semantics need to cross-check exact set
/// equality against a genesis evidence bundle's own claimed coverage. This
/// type is named distinctly from (and is not the same shape as) any future
/// `BLIND_CUSTODY`-category live reveal-package witness type owned
/// elsewhere; it does not construct, assign, seal, or reveal blind review
/// data itself, and does not claim to satisfy that other category's
/// `verify_blind_review_reveal` contract.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct VerifiedHistoricalReviewRevealV1 {
    private: VerifiedHistoricalReviewRevealFieldsV1,
}

impl VerifiedHistoricalReviewRevealV1 {
    #[cfg(test)]
    fn from_independent_verification(
        _seal: &IndependentAuthorityVerificationSealV1,
        fields: VerifiedHistoricalReviewRevealFieldsV1,
    ) -> Self {
        Self { private: fields }
    }

    fn matches_coverage(&self, coverage: &HistoricalBlindReviewCoverageV1) -> bool {
        let facts = &self.private;
        facts.assignment_hashes == coverage.assignment_hashes
            && facts.assignment_commitment_hashes == coverage.assignment_commitment_hashes
            && facts.sealed_review_hashes == coverage.sealed_review_hashes
            && facts.verified_reveal_hash == coverage.verified_reveal_hash
            && facts.reviewer_qualification_hashes == coverage.reviewer_qualification_hashes
            && facts.disposition_hashes == coverage.disposition_hashes
            && facts.reviewed_artifact_set_hash == coverage.reviewed_artifact_set_hash
    }
}

/// The exact three-root cycle-prevention set from the package currently being
/// verified, mirroring `commitment::CurrentPackageCommitments`. Kept as a
/// distinct trust-layer type so `trust.rs` never depends on package-private
/// commitment internals beyond the one frozen constructor call below.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ForbiddenCurrentGenesisRootsV1 {
    pub authorization_target_hash: ProtocolHash256,
    pub prepublication_root: ProtocolHash256,
    pub final_package_root: ProtocolHash256,
}

/// Opaque, cycle-free, always-non-retroactive result of genesis adoption
/// semantic verification.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct VerifiedGenesisAdoptionV1 {
    tenant_id: String,
    protocol_id: String,
    issuer_did: Did,
    receipt_root: ProtocolHash256,
}

/// Recomputes every chronology entry hash and predecessor link; requires
/// chronological order by `(occurred_at, act_kind, act_id)`; dereferences the
/// exact Git object and content hash for each chronology entry; proves exact
/// set equality among chronology, submitted, unchanged, assigned,
/// sealed-review, revealed, qualified, disposed, and reviewed artifacts;
/// verifies the signing payload under
/// `exo.decision_forum.genesis_adoption_signing_payload.v1`; resolves issuer
/// DID/key/role/tenant/protocol/version/scope/validity/revocation/conflict
/// only from `VerifiedGenesisIssuerAuthorityV1`. Semantic validation rejects
/// any of the three selected current-package ProtocolHash256 roots
/// (authorization_target_hash, prepublication_root, final_package_root)
/// appearing in the scanned genesis ProtocolHash256 fields, via the same
/// closed three-root set carried by ForbiddenCurrentGenesisRootsV1 /
/// CurrentPackageCommitments. A closeout-index root is a Slice 10 concept
/// and is not fabricated here.
pub fn verify_genesis_adoption_receipt_semantics(
    receipt: &GenesisAdoptionReceipt,
    chronology_artifacts: &BTreeMap<GitObjectId, VerifiedHistoricalArtifactV1>,
    review_evidence: &VerifiedHistoricalReviewRevealV1,
    issuer_authority: &VerifiedGenesisIssuerAuthorityV1,
    forbidden_current_roots: &ForbiddenCurrentGenesisRootsV1,
) -> Result<VerifiedGenesisAdoptionV1, ProtocolError> {
    let receipt_root = verify_genesis_adoption_receipt(
        receipt,
        CurrentPackageCommitments {
            authorization_target_hash: forbidden_current_roots.authorization_target_hash,
            prepublication_root: forbidden_current_roots.prepublication_root,
            final_package_root: forbidden_current_roots.final_package_root,
        },
    )?;

    let bundle = &receipt.evidence_bundle;
    for (index, entry) in bundle.chronology_entries.iter().enumerate() {
        let artifact = chronology_artifacts
            .get(&entry.git_object_id)
            .ok_or_else(|| {
                graph_mismatch(
                    format!(
                        "/receipt_manifest/genesis_adoption_receipt/evidence_bundle/chronology_entries/{index}/git_object_id"
                    ),
                    "independently dereferenced Git object",
                    entry.git_object_id.to_string(),
                )
            })?;
        if !artifact.matches(entry.artifact_content_hash, entry.artifact_path_hash) {
            return Err(graph_mismatch(
                format!(
                    "/receipt_manifest/genesis_adoption_receipt/evidence_bundle/chronology_entries/{index}/artifact_content_hash"
                ),
                "Git object content matching the claimed content and path hash",
                "dereferenced content mismatch",
            ));
        }
    }

    if !review_evidence.matches_coverage(&bundle.ordinary_blinded_review) {
        return Err(graph_mismatch(
            "/receipt_manifest/genesis_adoption_receipt/evidence_bundle/ordinary_blinded_review",
            "exact set equality with independently verified blind review reveal evidence",
            "claimed coverage does not match verified review evidence",
        ));
    }

    issuer_authority.verify_binding(receipt)?;

    Ok(VerifiedGenesisAdoptionV1 {
        tenant_id: receipt.tenant_id.clone(),
        protocol_id: receipt.protocol_id.clone(),
        issuer_did: receipt.issuer_did.clone(),
        receipt_root,
    })
}

/// Test-only construction of independently verified genesis evidence that
/// exactly matches a receipt's own chronology and blind-review coverage, so
/// mutation tests can isolate a single semantic check (for example, a forged
/// issuer key) without also tripping the artifact or review cross-checks.
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) fn verified_genesis_test_evidence(
    receipt: &GenesisAdoptionReceipt,
) -> (
    BTreeMap<GitObjectId, VerifiedHistoricalArtifactV1>,
    VerifiedHistoricalReviewRevealV1,
) {
    let seal = IndependentAuthorityVerificationSealV1(());
    let chronology_artifacts = receipt
        .evidence_bundle
        .chronology_entries
        .iter()
        .map(|entry| {
            (
                entry.git_object_id,
                VerifiedHistoricalArtifactV1::from_independent_verification(
                    &seal,
                    entry.artifact_content_hash,
                    entry.artifact_path_hash,
                ),
            )
        })
        .collect();
    let coverage = &receipt.evidence_bundle.ordinary_blinded_review;
    let review_evidence = VerifiedHistoricalReviewRevealV1::from_independent_verification(
        &seal,
        VerifiedHistoricalReviewRevealFieldsV1 {
            assignment_hashes: coverage.assignment_hashes.clone(),
            assignment_commitment_hashes: coverage.assignment_commitment_hashes.clone(),
            sealed_review_hashes: coverage.sealed_review_hashes.clone(),
            verified_reveal_hash: coverage.verified_reveal_hash,
            reviewer_qualification_hashes: coverage.reviewer_qualification_hashes.clone(),
            disposition_hashes: coverage.disposition_hashes.clone(),
            reviewed_artifact_set_hash: coverage.reviewed_artifact_set_hash,
        },
    );
    (chronology_artifacts, review_evidence)
}

/// Test-only construction of an independently verified genesis-issuer
/// authority that otherwise exactly matches the receipt, except for the
/// caller-supplied verification key. Used to prove a receipt signed by one
/// key is rejected when the independently resolved authority is bound to a
/// different key (a forged/mismatched issuer key).
#[cfg(test)]
pub(crate) fn verified_genesis_issuer_authority_with_key(
    receipt: &GenesisAdoptionReceipt,
    verification_key: Ed25519VerificationKey,
) -> VerifiedGenesisIssuerAuthorityV1 {
    let seal = IndependentAuthorityVerificationSealV1(());
    VerifiedGenesisIssuerAuthorityV1::from_independent_verification(
        &seal,
        VerifiedGenesisIssuerAuthorityFieldsV1 {
            tenant_id: receipt.tenant_id.clone(),
            protocol_id: receipt.protocol_id.clone(),
            protocol_version_hash: receipt.protocol_version_hash,
            issuer_did: receipt.issuer_did.clone(),
            scope: AuthorityScope::GenesisAdoptionReceiptV1,
            signing_key_id: receipt.issuer_key_id,
            verification_key,
            valid_from: Timestamp::new(0, 0),
            valid_until: Timestamp::new(1_000, 0),
            revocation_hash: None,
            conflict_disposition_hash: None,
        },
    )
}
```

Gate 10 adds this exact structural-authority boundary test. The independent
registry is created first. Changing `binding_mode` requires rebuilding the

```rust
fn rebuild_publication_and_final_root(package: &mut PeerReviewedProtocolPackageV1) {
    let publisher = KeyPair::from_secret_bytes([42; 32]).expect("fixture publisher key");
    let prepublication = prepublication_root(package).expect("recomputed prepublication root");
    let receipt = package
        .receipt_manifest
        .publication_authorization_receipt
        .as_mut()
        .expect("fixture publication receipt");
    receipt.prepublication_root = prepublication;
    receipt.signature.signature = Ed25519Signature::ZERO;
    receipt.signature.signed_payload_hash = ProtocolHash256::ZERO;
    let digest =
        publication_authorization_payload_hash(receipt).expect("publication signing payload");
    let Signature::Ed25519(bytes) = publisher.sign(digest.as_bytes()) else {
        panic!("fixture publisher uses Ed25519");
    };
    receipt.signature.signature = Ed25519Signature::from_bytes(bytes);
    receipt.signature.signed_payload_hash = digest;
    package.receipt_manifest.final_package_root = ProtocolHash256::ZERO;
    package.receipt_manifest.final_package_root =
        recompute_final_package_root(package).expect("recomputed final root");
}

#[test]
fn binding_shaped_package_is_structurally_accepted_but_never_authorizes() {
    let trust = fixture::independent_trust_context();
    let advisory = fixture::valid_v1_package();
    let advisory_root =
        verify_v1_package_root(&advisory, &trust).expect("advisory package is structurally valid");
    assert!(!advisory_root.grants_authority());

    let mut binding_shaped = advisory;
    binding_shaped.disposition_bundle.binding_mode = BindingMode::BindingInsideRatifiedEnvelope;
    rebuild_publication_and_final_root(&mut binding_shaped);

        .expect("binding-shaped evidence remains structurally verifiable");

        advisory_root.final_package_root(),

    );
}
```

```rust
fn frozen_quorum_domain_and_structural_binding_boundary_do_not_drift() {
```

Gate 10 starts with this complete graph-edge test. It invokes the Gate-10-owned
package-private `VerifiedPackageTrustRegistryV1::verify_package_graph` directly
with Gate-09 projection inputs. It does not call Gate 11's
`verify_package_root`. Gate 11 later composes structural/self-consistency checks
with this already-GREEN trusted-graph verifier:

```rust
fn assert_graph_error(
    baseline: &PeerReviewedProtocolPackageV1,
    trust: &VerifiedPackageTrustRegistryV1,
    mutate: impl FnOnce(&mut PeerReviewedProtocolPackageV1),
    expected_path: &str,
) {
    let mut candidate = baseline.clone();
    mutate(&mut candidate);
    let computed_version =
        protocol_version_hash(&candidate.protocol_identity).expect("candidate identity hash");
    let authorization =
        authorization_target_hash(&candidate).expect("candidate authorization target");
    let error = trust
        .verify_package_graph(&candidate, computed_version, authorization)
        .expect_err(expected_path);
    let actual_layer = match error {
        ProtocolError::CommitmentMismatch { component, .. } => component.to_owned(),
        ProtocolError::DuplicateIdentifier { collection, .. }
        | ProtocolError::InvalidOrder { collection, .. } => collection.to_owned(),
        ProtocolError::SignaturePayloadMismatch { target } => target.to_owned(),
        ProtocolError::CrossBinding { path, .. }
        | ProtocolError::GraphMismatch { path, .. }
        | ProtocolError::AuthorityChainMismatch { path, .. }
        | ProtocolError::Quorum { path, .. }
        | ProtocolError::Cardinality { path, .. } => path,
        other => panic!("{expected_path}: wrong error {other:?}"),
    };
    assert_eq!(actual_layer, expected_path);
}

#[test]
fn cross_binding_graph_rejects_rebound_and_early_failures_at_exact_layers() {
    let trust = fixture::independent_trust_context();
    let package = fixture::valid_v1_package();
    let computed_version =
        protocol_version_hash(&package.protocol_identity).expect("baseline identity hash");
    let authorization = authorization_target_hash(&package).expect("baseline target");
    trust
        .verify_package_graph(&package, computed_version, authorization)
        .expect("baseline graph");

    // These raw mutations intentionally do not rebuild hashes/signatures. This
    // Gate-10 test invokes the trusted graph directly and asserts the first
    // trust-owned JSON-pointer layer reached in deterministic verifier order.
    assert_graph_error(
        &package,
        &trust,
        |value| {
            value.review_bundle.assignments[0].blind_assignment_commitment =
                ProtocolHash256::ZERO;
        },
        "/review_bundle/assignments/*/context",
    );
    assert_graph_error(
        &package,
        &trust,

            value.review_bundle.assignments[1].assignment_id =
                value.review_bundle.assignments[0].assignment_id;

                value.review_bundle.signed_reviews[1].assignment_id;

    );

        &package,

            value.review_bundle.resolution_matrix[0].review_id =
                value.review_bundle.signed_reviews[1].review_id;
        },

    );
    assert_graph_error(

    assert_graph_error(

    assert_graph_error(

        },

    assert_graph_error(

            value.disposition_bundle.quorum_proofs[0].result = QuorumResult::NotUnanimous;
        },

    assert_graph_error(

    // Fully rebuilt/re-signed attacker graphs are exercised separately by the

}

#[test]
fn genesis_forged_issuer_key_rejected() {
    let version_hash = ProtocolHash256::from_bytes([71; 32]);
    let issuer_key = KeyPair::from_secret_bytes([67; 32]).expect("Gate-10 genesis issuer key");
    let forged_key = KeyPair::from_secret_bytes([68; 32]).expect("Gate-10 forged issuer key");
    let receipt = fixture::genesis_adoption_receipt(version_hash, &issuer_key);
    let (chronology_artifacts, review_evidence) = verified_genesis_test_evidence(&receipt);
    // The independently resolved authority is bound to a different key than
    // the one that actually produced the receipt's signature: a forged key.
    let issuer_authority = verified_genesis_issuer_authority_with_key(
        &receipt,
        Ed25519VerificationKey::from_bytes(*forged_key.public_key().as_bytes()),
    );
    let forbidden_current_roots = ForbiddenCurrentGenesisRootsV1 {
        authorization_target_hash: fixture::hash(180),
        prepublication_root: fixture::hash(181),
        final_package_root: fixture::hash(182),
    };
    let error = verify_genesis_adoption_receipt_semantics(
        &receipt,
        &chronology_artifacts,
        &review_evidence,
        &issuer_authority,
        &forbidden_current_roots,
    )
    .expect_err("forged issuer key must be rejected");
    match error {
        ProtocolError::GraphMismatch { path, .. } => {
            assert_eq!(
                path,
                "/receipt_manifest/genesis_adoption_receipt/issuer_did"
            );
        }
        other => panic!("expected GraphMismatch on issuer_did, got {other:?}"),
    }
}
```

The full fixture is binding-shaped but advisory in effect and populates every
optional/repeated family: nonempty datasets/resource ceilings/claim thresholds,
ten complete seat/signature contexts, ten assignments/reviews/responses/
revisions/resolutions, five Council votes, five AI-IRB votes, authorization and
monitoring dissents, every Chair choice/effect, two quorum proofs, genesis,
predecessor reference in the successor fixture, protocol events including

Gate 13 uses a recursive JSON-pointer enumerator over that fixture. It records
every object leaf and every array path, applies exactly one mutation, omission,
reorder, or duplicate operation, and requires strict decode rejection,
structural rejection, signature/context rejection, or a changed expected
commitment. It also asserts that the visited pointer set equals a checked-in
`AUTHORITATIVE_POINTERS_V1` constant; adding a field without adding its
expected layer fails the test. The constant contains every leaf, not component
counts. Separate cases cover every optional field in both `None` and populated
forms and every collection at length 0, 1, and its required full cardinality.

### One continuous cross-version receipt history

`VerifiedExecutionSegment` is a private verified-segment implementation detail. A separate opaque,
non-`Clone` `VerifiedExecutionHistory` owns the accepted tenant/protocol head,
accepted numeric package version, terminal sequence/hash/HLC, every accepted
receipt ID, every accepted idempotency hash, and every accepted segment root.
It has no public constructor. The only continuation API takes
`&mut VerifiedExecutionHistory`; it first proves that the opaque root is either
the exact package already at the accepted head or a strictly newer package
whose privately retained predecessor reference equals the history's current
exact `successor_chain_reference`. It then verifies the candidate completely
and advances the head atomically in memory only after all checks pass. The
public chain builder performs the same lineage check before constructing a
segment. Slice 4 persists the same compare-and-swap invariant transactionally.

```rust
pub fn begin_execution_history(
    genesis_package: &PeerReviewedProtocolPackageV1,
    segment: &ProtocolExecutionReceiptChainV1,
    verified_root: &VerifiedPackageRoot,
    signer_authorities: &VerifiedAuthorityRegistryV1,
) -> Result<VerifiedExecutionHistory, ProtocolError>;

pub fn verify_and_advance_execution_history(
    history: &mut VerifiedExecutionHistory,
    verified_current_root: &VerifiedPackageRoot,
    segment: &ProtocolExecutionReceiptChainV1,
    signer_authorities: &VerifiedAuthorityRegistryV1,
) -> Result<(), ProtocolError>;

pub fn successor_chain_reference(
    history: &VerifiedExecutionHistory,
) -> PriorExecutionReceiptChainReferenceV1;
```

For same-package continuation, tenant, protocol, numeric package version,
protocol-version hash, and package root must all equal the accepted head. For a
package transition, tenant/protocol must match, the numeric version must be
strictly greater than the accepted version, and the opaque root's privately
stored predecessor reference must equal every field of
`successor_chain_reference(history)`. A v2 segment then starts at the v1
terminal sequence plus one and links its first receipt to the v1 terminal
receipt hash while carrying the newly recomputed v2 protocol-version hash and
v2 package root. Requiring the transitioned package version/root to equal the
predecessor version/root is forbidden. The opaque lineage fact—not an
independently supplied root plus history pair—proves which predecessor verified
the successor package; the segment and all its receipts name that verified
current root.

Before scanning a candidate segment, verify the root/history lineage and clone the history's private ID,
idempotency, receipt-hash, and segment-root sets into local working sets. A
duplicate against either prior history or the candidate returns
`ReceiptReplay` with kind/value/path. Require the candidate's predecessor head
to equal the history's currently accepted head. After one successor advances
the history, submitting a stale successor root whose private lineage still
names the old head returns `PredecessorMismatch` before any set or head changes.
Submitting a different same-package segment whose receipt chain still names the
old head returns `ReceiptFork`; a broken link inside one segment is only
`ReceiptLinkMismatch` and is not accepted as fork evidence. Every rejection
test compares a deterministic debug-byte snapshot of all private history state
before and after the call.

Gate 16 RED/GREEN commands select the real lineage-rejection body and the
existing positive v2 continuation body:

```bash
cargo test -p exochain-decision-forum --lib \
  protocol::receipt::history::tests::root_history_lineage_rejects_disconnected_rebound_and_other_history_without_mutation \
  -- --exact --nocapture 2>&1 | tee "$LOG"
cargo test -p exochain-decision-forum --lib \
  protocol::receipt::history::tests::v2_continues_v1_sequence_and_hash_with_new_version_and_root \
  -- --exact --nocapture 2>&1 | tee "$LOG"
```

Gate 17's selected test preserves predecessor ID reuse, predecessor
idempotency-hash reuse, and two correctly signed same-package segments from one
head, and adds a separately verified stale successor root after another
successor has advanced the head. The accepted transition passes; replay,
stale-root, and second-segment calls return their exact typed failures and leave
the history snapshot unchanged. The exact RED/GREEN command selects
`history_rejects_replay_stale_successor_and_second_segment_without_mutation`.

### Full actual-output cross-implementation vectors

Replace the probe-only vector with committed, schema-valid input fixtures for
the complete `AuthorizationTargetV1`, `PrepublicationPackageV1`, verified
publication-authorization signing body, normalized final package,
`GenesisEvidenceBundleV1`/adoption receipt, renderer manifest, external artifact
manifest, and a two-version receipt history. Rust and pinned TypeScript each
emit normalized JSONL containing canonical-CBOR hex and domain root for every
named object plus final package roots and both segment/history heads. The
comparison checks exact keys and exact values, never a result count.

The vector interchange represents every `u64` as an exact decimal string.
Rust parses with `str::parse::<u64>()`; TypeScript parses with `BigInt(text)` and
the canonical encoder accepts `bigint` directly. It rejects a number-valued
`physical_ms`, `Number(...)`, `parseInt`, unary `+`, and any value outside
`0..=0xffffffffffffffffn`. Include HLC vectors at `9007199254740991`,
`9007199254740992`, and `18446744073709551615` to prove no JavaScript safe-
integer narrowing.

```typescript
function u64(text: string, path: string): bigint {
  if (!/^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/.test(text)) throw new Error(`${path}: noncanonical u64`);
  const value = BigInt(text);
  if (value > 0xffffffffffffffffn) throw new Error(`${path}: u64 overflow`);
  return value;
}

function encode(value: unknown): Buffer {
  if (typeof value === 'bigint') return header(0, value);
  if (typeof value === 'number') {
    if (!Number.isSafeInteger(value) || value < 0) {
      throw new Error('number must be a nonnegative safe structural integer');
    }
    return header(0, BigInt(value));
  }
  // The remaining null/bool/bytes/text/array/canonical-map arms are the exact
  // arms in the complete Gate 19 executor below.
  throw new Error(`unsupported canonical CBOR type ${typeof value}`);
}
```

The comment in this excerpt does not replace code: the final `index.ts` block
must retain the complete existing encoder arms and replace only its integer arm
with the two exact arms above. `rust_emits_exact_production_commitment_outputs` asserts the
output-key set equals:

```text
authorization_target,protocol_version,protocol_envelope,review_bundle,
council_eligible_set,ai_irb_eligible_set,prepublication,
publication_authorization,normalized_final,final_package_root,
genesis_evidence,genesis_adoption,renderer_manifest,
publication_artifact_manifest,v1_receipt_segment,v2_receipt_segment,
accepted_receipt_chain_root
```

The eligible-set rows serialize the exact `(SeatKind, eligible_set)` production
projection; the publication row serializes
`PublicationAuthorizationSigningPayloadV1::from(receipt)`; the genesis row
serializes the receipt after only `receipt_root` is zeroed; and both execution
segment rows serialize the chain after only `chain_root` is zeroed. The final
history row is the scalar recomputed/verified v2 `chain_root` accepted by Rust
and independently recomputed by TypeScript. No history object is invented and
no existing hash domain is applied to an ad hoc history shape.

The golden vector is generated only by the reviewed Rust implementation, then
the test independently recomputes and compares it in Rust and TypeScript.
Neither runner may read `expected` values as its `actual` output. The unit test
removes, duplicates, and forges each named record in turn and requires the
comparison to fail.

For Gates 01-18 and 20, run this exact base/write-test/RED/GREEN/list/stage/commit
contract after setting the manifest values. Gate 19 uses the TypeScript variant
immediately below. `GATE_PATHS` is the literal
space-delimited required allowlist in that gate's row; no glob or directory
broader than the row is permitted. Bracketed `Cargo.lock only when changed` is
the sole conditional path in the manifest; unchanged optional paths are never
required or staged:

```bash
test -z "$(git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all)"
test "$(git branch --show-current)" = "bob-stewart/df-protocol-001-02-core-model"
REPORT_DIR=.superpowers/sdd/reports/df-protocol-001
GATE_ID=01
GATE_TEST_TARGET=df_protocol_001_wire
GATE_TEST_NAME=fixed_bytes_are_hex_in_json_and_bytes_in_cbor
GATE_TEST_FILE=crates/decision-forum/tests/df_protocol_001_wire.rs
GATE_RED_PATTERN='unresolved import|cannot find|failed'
GATE_REQUIRED_PATHS='crates/decision-forum/Cargo.toml crates/decision-forum/src/lib.rs crates/decision-forum/src/protocol/mod.rs crates/decision-forum/src/protocol/error.rs crates/decision-forum/src/protocol/codec/mod.rs crates/decision-forum/src/protocol/codec/fixed_bytes.rs crates/decision-forum/src/protocol/codec/cbor.rs crates/decision-forum/tests/df_protocol_001_wire.rs'
GATE_OPTIONAL_PATHS='Cargo.lock'
GATE_COMMIT='feat(decision-forum): add fixed protocol wire bytes'
GATE_BASE_FILE="$REPORT_DIR/02-core-model-gate-${GATE_ID}-base.txt"
test ! -e "$GATE_BASE_FILE"
GATE_BASE="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
GATE_TREE="$(git rev-parse HEAD^{tree})"
printf 'commit=%s\ntree=%s\n' "$GATE_BASE" "$GATE_TREE" > "$GATE_BASE_FILE"
PROGRESS=.superpowers/sdd/progress.md
PROGRESS_LOCK="$PROGRESS.append-lock"
PROGRESS_LOCK_PENDING="$PROGRESS_LOCK.pending.$$"
acquire_progress_writer_lock() {
  local owner snapshot iteration=1
  while test "$iteration" -le 25; do
    (umask 077; printf '%s\n' "$$" > "$PROGRESS_LOCK_PENDING") || return 1
    if ln "$PROGRESS_LOCK_PENDING" "$PROGRESS_LOCK" 2>/dev/null; then
      rm -f "$PROGRESS_LOCK_PENDING" || return 1
      return 0
    fi
    rm -f "$PROGRESS_LOCK_PENDING" || return 1
    if test ! -e "$PROGRESS_LOCK" && test ! -L "$PROGRESS_LOCK"; then
      sleep 0.01 || return 1
      iteration=$((iteration + 1))
      continue
    fi
    test -f "$PROGRESS_LOCK" || return 1
    test ! -L "$PROGRESS_LOCK" || return 1
    IFS= read -r owner < "$PROGRESS_LOCK" || return 1
    case "$owner" in *[!0-9]*|'') return 1 ;; esac
    if ! kill -0 "$owner" 2>/dev/null; then
      snapshot="$PROGRESS_LOCK.stale.$$"
      if ln "$PROGRESS_LOCK" "$snapshot" 2>/dev/null; then
        if test "$PROGRESS_LOCK" -ef "$snapshot"; then
          rm -f "$PROGRESS_LOCK" || return 1
        fi
        rm -f "$snapshot" || return 1
      fi
    fi
    sleep 0.01 || return 1
    iteration=$((iteration + 1))
  done
  return 1
}
release_progress_writer_lock() {
  local owner
  test -f "$PROGRESS_LOCK" || return 1
  test ! -L "$PROGRESS_LOCK" || return 1
  IFS= read -r owner < "$PROGRESS_LOCK" || return 1
  test "$owner" = "$$" || return 1
  rm -f "$PROGRESS_LOCK" || return 1
}
acquire_progress_writer_lock
printf 'DF-PROTOCOL-001 slice 2 gate %s base %s tree %s\n' \
  "$GATE_ID" "$GATE_BASE" "$GATE_TREE" >> "$PROGRESS"
release_progress_writer_lock
git add "$GATE_BASE_FILE" .superpowers/sdd/progress.md
git diff --cached --check
git commit -m "chore: record slice 2 gate ${GATE_ID} base"
test "$(git show HEAD:"$GATE_BASE_FILE" | sed -n 's/^commit=//p')" = "$GATE_BASE"
test "$(git show HEAD:"$GATE_BASE_FILE" | sed -n 's/^tree=//p')" = "$GATE_TREE"

# Write the gate's complete RED test body now, after the immutable base record.
# The direct body read is required because a new untracked test has no ordinary
# `git diff` output. The Git disposition branch proves whether the owner is a
# new untracked path or a tracked predecessor path without mutating the index.
GATE_TEST_SYMBOL="${GATE_TEST_NAME##*::}"
test -s "$GATE_TEST_FILE"
rg -n "fn ${GATE_TEST_SYMBOL}\\(" "$GATE_TEST_FILE"
if git ls-files --error-unmatch -- "$GATE_TEST_FILE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  test -n "$(git diff -- "$GATE_TEST_FILE")"
  git diff -- "$GATE_TEST_FILE" | rg -n "fn ${GATE_TEST_SYMBOL}\\("
else
  test -z "$(git ls-files -- "$GATE_TEST_FILE")"
  test "$(git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all -- "$GATE_TEST_FILE")" = \
    "?? $GATE_TEST_FILE"
fi
set +e
cargo test -p exochain-decision-forum --test "$GATE_TEST_TARGET" \
  "$GATE_TEST_NAME" -- --exact --nocapture \
  > "$REPORT_DIR/logs/02-gate-${GATE_ID}-red.log" 2>&1
RED_STATUS=$?
set -e
test "$RED_STATUS" -ne 0
rg -n "$GATE_RED_PATTERN" "$REPORT_DIR/logs/02-gate-${GATE_ID}-red.log"
```

```bash
  git diff -- "$GATE_TEST_FILE" | rg -n "fn ${GATE_TEST_SYMBOL}\\("
else
  test -z "$(git ls-files -- "$GATE_TEST_FILE")"
  test "$(git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all -- "$GATE_TEST_FILE")" = \
    "?? $GATE_TEST_FILE"
fi
set +e
cargo test -p exochain-decision-forum --lib \
  "$GATE_TEST_NAME" -- --exact --nocapture \
  > "$REPORT_DIR/logs/02-gate-${GATE_ID}-red.log" 2>&1
RED_STATUS=$?
set -e
test "$RED_STATUS" -ne 0
rg -n "$GATE_RED_PATTERN" "$REPORT_DIR/logs/02-gate-${GATE_ID}-red.log"
cargo test -p exochain-decision-forum --lib \
  "$GATE_TEST_NAME" -- --exact --nocapture \
  2>&1 | tee "$REPORT_DIR/logs/02-gate-${GATE_ID}-green.log"
TEST_LIST="$(cargo test -p exochain-decision-forum --lib -- --list)"
test "$(printf '%s\n' "$TEST_LIST" | rg -c "^${GATE_TEST_NAME}: test$")" -eq 1
cargo test -p exochain-decision-forum --lib -- --nocapture \
  2>&1 | tee "$REPORT_DIR/logs/02-gate-${GATE_ID}-suite.log"
```

Gate 19 uses the same immutable base and stage/range portions. After that base
commit, write `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `tsconfig.json`, and the
complete `index.test.ts` body while leaving the new `executeFull` and
`executeRenderer` exports absent. The RED is therefore the expected TypeScript
compile failure, not an impossible pre-GREEN typecheck. Both RED and GREEN run
only in a trap-cleaned temporary copy; the repository is checked for residue
before and after:

```bash
test ! -e tools/cross-impl-test/node_modules
test ! -e tools/cross-impl-test/dist
test -s tools/cross-impl-test/index.test.ts
if git ls-files --error-unmatch -- tools/cross-impl-test/index.test.ts >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  test -n "$(git diff -- tools/cross-impl-test/index.test.ts)"
else
  test "$(git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all -- \
    tools/cross-impl-test/index.test.ts)" = \
    "?? tools/cross-impl-test/index.test.ts"
fi
test "$(rg -c '^test\(' tools/cross-impl-test/index.test.ts)" -ge 10
TMP_ROOT="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/df-slice2-gate19.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP_ROOT"' EXIT INT TERM
cp tools/cross-impl-test/package.json \
  tools/cross-impl-test/package-lock.json \
  tools/cross-impl-test/tsconfig.json \
  tools/cross-impl-test/index.ts \
  tools/cross-impl-test/index.test.ts "$TMP_ROOT/"
(cd "$TMP_ROOT" && npm ci --ignore-scripts)
set +e
(cd "$TMP_ROOT" && npm run typecheck) \
  > "$REPORT_DIR/logs/02-gate-19-red.log" 2>&1
RED_STATUS=$?
set -e
test "$RED_STATUS" -ne 0
rg -n 'executeFull|executeRenderer|has no exported member' \
  "$REPORT_DIR/logs/02-gate-19-red.log"

# Apply the complete Gate-19 GREEN owners, refresh only the temporary copy,
# then typecheck, compile, run the Node tests, and compare both real Rust
# executors with the TypeScript executor.
cp tools/cross-impl-test/index.ts \
  tools/cross-impl-test/index.test.ts \
  tools/cross-impl-test/compare.sh \
  tools/cross-impl-test/compare_unit_test.sh "$TMP_ROOT/"
(cd "$TMP_ROOT" && npm run typecheck)
(cd "$TMP_ROOT" && npm test) \
  2>&1 | tee "$REPORT_DIR/logs/02-gate-19-green.log"
EXO_TS_ROOT="$TMP_ROOT" bash tools/cross-impl-test/compare.sh --verbose \
  2>&1 | tee "$REPORT_DIR/logs/02-gate-19-suite.log"
EXO_TS_ROOT="$TMP_ROOT" bash tools/cross-impl-test/compare_unit_test.sh
rm -rf "$TMP_ROOT"
trap - EXIT INT TERM
test ! -e tools/cross-impl-test/node_modules
test ! -e tools/cross-impl-test/dist
```

```rust
fn gate_03_identity() -> ProtocolIdentity {
    let chair_did = Did::parse("did:exo:chair").expect("Gate-03 fixture DID");
    ProtocolIdentity {
        protocol_id: "DF-PROTOCOL-001".to_owned(),
        tenant_id: "tenant-a".to_owned(),
        constitutional_hash: ProtocolHash256::from_bytes([1; 32]),
        version: 1,
        prior_version_hash: None,
        lifecycle_state: exo_core::bcts::BctsState::Draft,
        co_pi_dids: std::collections::BTreeSet::from([
            Did::parse("did:exo:copi-human").expect("Gate-03 human Co-PI DID"),
            Did::parse("did:exo:copi-ai").expect("Gate-03 AI Co-PI DID"),
        ]),
        chair_did: chair_did.clone(),
        chair_authority: ChairAuthorityV1 {
            chair_did,
            signing_key_id: ProtocolHash256::from_bytes([2; 32]),
            verification_key: Ed25519VerificationKey::from_bytes([3; 32]),
            authority_chain_hash: ProtocolHash256::from_bytes([4; 32]),
        },
        domain: "decision-forum".to_owned(),
    }
}

#[test]

    let encoded = serde_json::to_value(&identity).expect("identity JSON");
    let decoded: ProtocolIdentity = serde_json::from_value(encoded).expect("identity round trip");
    assert_eq!(decoded, identity);
    assert_eq!(decoded.protocol_id, "DF-PROTOCOL-001");
    assert_eq!(decoded.co_pi_dids.len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(decoded.chair_did, decoded.chair_authority.chair_did);
}

        conflict_commitment: ProtocolHash256::from_bytes([17; 32]),

        review_id,
        assignment_id,
        protocol_version_hash: version_hash,
        criteria_results_hash: ProtocolHash256::from_bytes([17; 32]),
        review_body_hash: ProtocolHash256::from_bytes([18; 32]),
        disposition: PeerReviewDisposition::Approve,

            signature: Ed25519Signature::from_bytes([21; 64]),
            signed_payload_hash: ProtocolHash256::from_bytes([22; 32]),

            .expect("Gate-04 resolution UUID"),
        review_id,
        comment_hash: ProtocolHash256::from_bytes([23; 32]),
        author_response_hash: ProtocolHash256::from_bytes([24; 32]),
        revision_diff_hash: ProtocolHash256::from_bytes([25; 32]),
        resolution: ReviewResolutionKind::Accepted,
        resolved_at: ProtocolHlc::new(12, 0),

    assert_eq!(review.assignment_id, assignment.assignment_id);
```
